   204	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   205	# Reading and validating applied state (read-only, nonmutating)
   206	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   207	
   208	
   209	def read_schema_migrations(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> tuple[AppliedMigration, ...]:
   210	    """Read every ``schema_migrations`` row, or ``()`` when the table is absent."""
   211	    try:
   212	        cursor = conn.execute(
   213	            "SELECT pack, version, name, checksum, applied_at"
   214	            " FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY pack, version"
   215	        )
   216	    except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:
   217	        if "no such table" in str(exc):
   218	            return ()
   219	        raise
   220	    rows = cursor.fetchall()
   221	    return tuple(
   222	        AppliedMigration(
   223	            pack=row[0],
   224	            version=row[1],
   225	            name=row[2],
   226	            checksum=row[3],
   227	            applied_at=row[4],
   228	        )
   229	        for row in rows
   230	    )
   231	
   232	
   233	def _validate_applied_migrations(
   234	    applied: tuple[AppliedMigration, ...],
   235	    registry: FrozenSchemaPackRegistry,
   236	) -> None:
   237	    """Reject too-new schemas, name drift, and checksum drift (no mutation)."""
   238	    per_pack: dict[str, list[AppliedMigration]] = {}
   239	    for row in applied:
   240	        per_pack.setdefault(row.pack, []).append(row)
   241	
   242	    for pack_id in sorted(per_pack):
   243	        rows = sorted(per_pack[pack_id], key=lambda row: row.version)
   244	        if pack_id not in registry.packs:
   245	            raise MigrationTooNewError(
   246	                "database contains applied migrations for pack "
   247	                f"{pack_id!r}, which is not registered in this composition"
   248	            )
   249	        max_version = max(
   250	            (m.version for m in registry.migrations if m.pack == pack_id),
   251	            default=0,
   252	        )
   253	        for row in rows:
   254	            if row.version > max_version:
   255	                raise MigrationTooNewError(
   256	                    f"database schema for pack {pack_id!r} is too new: "
   257	                    f"applied version {row.version} exceeds the highest "
   258	                    f"registered version {max_version}"
   259	                )
   260	            registered = registry.migration(pack_id, row.version)
   261	            if registered is None:
   262	                raise MigrationError(
   263	                    f"applied migration {pack_id}/{row.version} has no "
   264	                    "registered descriptor in this composition"
   265	                )
   266	            if registered.name != row.name:
   267	                raise MigrationNameDriftError(
   268	                    f"migration name drift for {pack_id}/{row.version}: "
   269	                    f"database records name {row.name!r}, registry declares "
   270	                    f"{registered.name!r}"
   271	                )
   272	            expected = sha256_bytes(read_migration_bytes(registered))
   273	            if expected != row.checksum:
   274	                raise MigrationChecksumDriftError(
   275	                    f"migration checksum drift for {pack_id}/{row.version} "
   276	                    f"({registered.name}): database records {row.checksum}, "
   277	                    f"registered file bytes hash to {expected}"
   278	                )
   279	
   280	
   281	def read_only_uri(db_path: Path) -> str:
   282	    """Return a read-only SQLite URI for *db_path*.
   283	
   284	    A database whose header declares WAL format but whose ``-wal``/``-shm``
   285	    sidecars do not exist (a freshly pragma-switched or copied snapshot) can
   286	    never be opened ``mode=ro`` — SQLite must create the ``-shm`` index,
   287	    which read-only opens cannot do. Because no ``-wal`` exists, the main
   288	    file is complete and quiescent, so ``immutable=1`` reads it directly and
   289	    correctly. Whenever a ``-wal`` exists the normal ``mode=ro`` open is used
   290	    so committed WAL content is still visible.
   291	    """
   292	    header = db_path.read_bytes()[:20]
   293	    wal_format = len(header) >= 20 and header[18] == 2  # file-format read version
   294	    has_wal = Path(f"{db_path}-wal").exists()
   295	    has_shm = Path(f"{db_path}-shm").exists()
   296	    if wal_format and not has_wal and not has_shm:
   297	        return f"file:{db_path}?immutable=1"
   298	    return f"file:{db_path}?mode=ro"
   299	
   300	
   301	def probe_database(
   302	    path: str | Path,
   303	    registry: FrozenSchemaPackRegistry,
   304	) -> DatabaseProbe:
   305	    """Probe a database read-only and reject incompatible applied state.
   306	
   307	    This is the nonmutating too-new probe: the database is opened with
   308	    ``mode=ro``, no PRAGMA is written, and no transaction is started. An
   309	    absent file is a fresh database with no applied migrations. Incompatible
   310	    state raises :class:`MigrationTooNewError`, :class:`MigrationNameDriftError`,
   311	    or :class:`MigrationChecksumDriftError` before any write is possible.
   312	    """
   313	    db_path = Path(path)
   314	    if not db_path.exists():
   315	        return DatabaseProbe(path=db_path, exists=False, applied=())
   316	    conn = sqlite3.connect(read_only_uri(db_path), uri=True, isolation_level=None)
   317	    try:
   318	        applied = read_schema_migrations(conn)
   319	    finally:
   320	        conn.close()
   321	    _validate_applied_migrations(applied, registry)
   322	    return DatabaseProbe(path=db_path, exists=True, applied=applied)
   323	
   324	
   325	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   326	# Statement splitting and transactional application
   327	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   328	
   329	
   330	def _split_sql_statements(sql: str) -> list[str]:
   331	    """Split one SQL script into statements on ``;`` outside string literals.
   332	
   333	    Full-line ``--`` comments are skipped and single-quoted strings (with the
   334	    SQLite ``''`` escape) are preserved. The shipped migration files are
   335	    simple DDL with no semicolons inside string literals; the state machine
   336	    keeps the splitter correct even if that invariant is ever broken.
   337	    """
   338	    statements: list[str] = []
   339	    current: list[str] = []
   340	    in_string = False
   341	    index = 0
   342	    length = len(sql)
   343	    while index < length:
   344	        char = sql[index]
   345	        if in_string:
   346	            current.append(char)
   347	            if char == "'":
   348	                if index + 1 < length and sql[index + 1] == "'":
   349	                    current.append(sql[index + 1])
   350	                    index += 1
   351	                else:
   352	                    in_string = False
   353	            index += 1
   354	            continue
   355	        if char == "'":
   356	            in_string = True
   357	            current.append(char)
   358	            index += 1
   359	            continue
   360	        if char == "-" and index + 1 < length and sql[index + 1] == "-":
   361	            while index < length and sql[index] != "\n":
   362	                index += 1
   363	            continue
   364	        if char == ";":
   365	            statement = "".join(current).strip()
   366	            if statement:
   367	                statements.append(statement)
   368	            current = []
   369	            index += 1
   370	            continue
   371	        current.append(char)
   372	        index += 1
   373	    tail = "".join(current).strip()
   374	    if tail:
   375	        statements.append(tail)
   376	    return statements
   377	
   378	
   379	def _is_pragma_statement(statement: str) -> bool:
   380	    return statement.lstrip().upper().startswith("PRAGMA")
   381	
   382	
   383	def _utc_now() -> str:
   384	    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
   385	
   386	
   387	def apply_pending_migrations(
   388	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
   389	    registry: FrozenSchemaPackRegistry,
   390	    probe: DatabaseProbe,
   391	) -> tuple[AppliedMigration, ...]:
   392	    """Apply every pending registered migration exactly once, transactionally.
   393	
   394	    Each pending migration runs inside its own ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` transaction:
   395	    its DDL/DML statements and the ``schema_migrations`` row commit together or
   396	    roll back together. PRAGMA statements (which cannot change inside a
   397	    transaction) run before ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE``. Already-applied versions are
   398	    skipped, so reopening a migrated database is a no-op.
   399	    """
   400	    applied_keys = {(row.pack, row.version) for row in probe.applied}
   401	    recorded: list[AppliedMigration] = []
   402	    for registered in topological_migration_order(registry):
   403	        key = (registered.pack, registered.version)
   404	        if key in applied_keys:
   405	            continue
   406	        sql_bytes = read_migration_bytes(registered)
   407	        checksum = sha256_bytes(sql_bytes)
   408	        statements = _split_sql_statements(sql_bytes.decode("utf-8"))
   409	        pragma_statements = [
   410	            statement
   411	            for statement in statements
   412	            if _is_pragma_statement(statement)
   413	        ]
   414	        ddl_statements = [
   415	            statement
   416	            for statement in statements
   417	            if not _is_pragma_statement(statement)
   418	        ]
   419	        applied_at = _utc_now()
   420	
   421	        for statement in pragma_statements:
   422	            conn.execute(statement)
   423	
   424	        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
   425	        try:
   426	            for statement in ddl_statements:
   427	                conn.execute(statement)
   428	            conn.execute(
   429	                "INSERT INTO schema_migrations"
   430	                " (pack, version, name, checksum, applied_at)"
   431	                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
   432	                (
   433	                    registered.pack,
   434	                    registered.version,
   435	                    registered.name,
   436	                    checksum,
   437	                    applied_at,
   438	                ),
   439	            )
   440	            conn.execute("COMMIT")
   441	        except sqlite3.Error as exc:
   442	            if conn.in_transaction:
   443	                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
   444	            raise MigrationApplyError(
   445	                f"migration {registered.pack}/{registered.version} "
   446	                f"({registered.name}) failed: {exc}"
   447	            ) from exc
   448	        recorded.append(
   449	            AppliedMigration(
   450	                pack=registered.pack,
   451	                version=registered.version,
   452	                name=registered.name,
   453	                checksum=checksum,
   454	                applied_at=applied_at,
   455	            )
   456	        )
   457	    return tuple(recorded)
   458

     1	"""Core stream, event, and command vocabulary with independent registration.
     2	
     3	(m1 plan step 2; m2 plan step 1.) The kernel registers its own vocabulary
     4	independently of any Astrid pack: core declares the ``core.project``,
     5	``core.task``, ``core.run``, and ``core.media`` stream types plus the m1/m2
     6	core event/command kinds, and only then may the explicit standard-Astrid
     7	composition in ``astrid/packs/__init__.py`` register the three in-tree schema
     8	packs (v10 section 2.3 law 5; decision artifact section 4).
     9	
    10	Rules kept here:
    11	
    12	- Vocabulary names are namespaced dotted names; the composed registry rejects
    13	  missing, duplicate, or non-namespaced declarations before any database opens.
    14	- The kernel has no ``schema-pack.yaml`` file: its manifest is code-declared by
    15	  :func:`core_schema_pack_manifest` and reuses
    16	  ``astrid.core.migrations.catalog.CORE_MIGRATIONS`` as the single audited
    17	  source for the core migration descriptor, so registry table ownership and the
    18	  migration runner can never drift.
    19	- This module never opens a database and never imports the capability-pack
    20	  loader, discovery, or definition machinery (v10 section 2 "Boundary now,
    21	  loader later").
    22	- Heartbeat deliberately gets no command or event kind: it is the narrow
    23	  non-event attempt-liveness exception (v10 section 5.1), so no heartbeat name
    24	  may ever appear in the core vocabulary.
    25	
    26	``core.task``, ``core.run``, and ``core.media`` stream types are registered now
    27	because v10 section 2.3 requires core to register its stream types; m1
    28	implements the project vertical only, so m1 core event/command kinds are the
    29	project ones. m2 (plan step 1) registers the exact task lifecycle (admission,
    30	claim, start, expiry, cancellation, failure, retry, completion), run fan-out
    31	and group, and media (import, location replacement, relations) command/event
    32	kinds the m2 repositories consume. m3 (plan step 1) adds the receipt-linked
    33	run continuation vocabulary (``core.run.continue``/``core.run.continued``),
    34	the kernel evidence event (``core.evidence.recorded``) and its receipt
    35	command kind (``core.evidence.record``), and registers
    36	aggregate agreement rules for the references and shots packs' own stream
    37	types (``reference.reference``, ``shot.shot``) so pack-owned repositories
    38	can create and write their aggregate streams without kernel DDL changes.
    39	"""

   233	# Runtime vocabulary enforcement (m1 plan step 8)
   234	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   235	#
   236	# These guards run before any SQL mutation. The frozen registry is the single
   237	# source of which stream types, event kinds, and command kinds exist; the
   238	# aggregate/type/project agreement rules below are the single, centrally
   239	# defined statement of what each *declared* stream type means. Repository
   240	# handlers never carry their own allowlists, so a handler can neither admit
   241	# an undeclared name nor redefine the meaning of a declared stream type.
   242	
   243	_NAMESPACED_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$")
   244	"""Namespaced (dotted) vocabulary name, matching the manifest grammar."""
   245

   247	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
   248	class StreamAggregateRule:
   249	    """Aggregate/type/project agreement for one declared stream type.
   250	
   251	    - ``subject_type`` is the ``events.subject_type`` every event on the
   252	      stream must carry; ``subject_id`` must equal the stream's aggregate id.
   253	    - ``aggregate_is_project`` marks streams whose aggregate is the project
   254	      itself (``core.project``): for these, the aggregate id must equal the
   255	      project id, so one project owns exactly one such stream.
   256	    """

   258	    stream_type: str
   259	    declaring_pack: str
   260	    subject_type: str

   260	        help="Output as a human-readable text table.",
   261	    )
   262	    agent_index_parser.set_defaults(handler=_handle_agent_index)
   263	
   264	    # ── search ──
   265	    search_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
   266	        "search",
   267	        help="Search packs by keyword/capability/purpose (ranked).",
   268	    )
   269	    search_parser.add_argument(
   270	        "query",
   271	        nargs="+",
   272	        help="One or more search terms (matched against id, name, "
   273	        "description, keywords, capabilities, and purpose).",
   274	    )
   275	    search_parser.add_argument(
   276	        "--limit",
   277	        type=int,
   278	        default=20,
   279	        help="Maximum results to show (default: 20; <=0 for all).",
   280	    )
   281	    search_parser.add_argument(
   282	        "--json",
   283	        action="store_true",
   284	        help="Emit machine-readable JSON.",
   285	    )
   286	    search_parser.set_defaults(handler=_handle_search)
   287	
   288	    return parser

    37	def _inspect_installed_pack(*, pack_id: str, agent: bool, json_output: bool) -> int:
    38	    """Render installed-pack inspect output for the public wrapper and CLI."""
    39	    from astrid.core.pack.store import InstalledPackStore
    40	
    41	    store = InstalledPackStore()
    42	    record = store.get_active(pack_id)
    43	
    44	    if record is None:
    45	        raise AstridError(
    46	            f"inspect: pack {pack_id!r} is not installed.",
    47	            recovery_command=f"Install the pack first: python3 -m astrid packs install {pack_id}",
    48	        )
    49	
    50	    rev_dir = store.active_revision_path(pack_id)
    51	    if rev_dir is None:
    52	        raise AstridError(
    53	            f"inspect: cannot resolve active revision for {pack_id!r}.",
    54	            recovery_command=f"Try reinstalling the pack: python3 -m astrid packs install {pack_id}",
    55	        )
    56	
    57	    manifest_path = pack_manifest_path(rev_dir)
    58	    if manifest_path is None:
    59	        raise AstridError(
    60	            f"inspect: no pack manifest found in installed revision {rev_dir}.",
    61	            recovery_command=f"The installed revision may be corrupt. Try reinstalling: python3 -m astrid packs install {pack_id}",
    62	        )
    63	
    64	    try:
    65	        manifest = load_manifest_mapping(manifest_path, manifest_kind="pack")
    66	    except ManifestParseError as e:
    67	        raise AstridError(
    68	            f"inspect: failed to parse pack manifest: {e}",
    69	            recovery_command=f"Check the manifest file for syntax errors: cat {manifest_path}",
    70	        ) from e
    71	
    72	    try:
    73	        trust_summary = extract_trust_summary(rev_dir)
    74	    except Exception:
    75	        trust_summary = {}
    76	
    77	    if agent:
    78	        agent_data = _build_agent_view(manifest, trust_summary)
    79	        if json_output:
    80	            print(json.dumps(agent_data, indent=2, default=str))
    81	        else:
    82	            _print_agent_view(agent_data)
    83	        return 0
    84	
    85	    full_data = _build_full_inspect(record, manifest, trust_summary, rev_dir=rev_dir)
    86	    if json_output:
    87	        print(json.dumps(full_data, indent=2, default=str))
    88	    else:
    89	        _print_full_inspect(full_data)
    90	
    91	    return 0
    92

    94	def cmd_inspect(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    95	    """Show details for an installed pack.
    96	
    97	    Usage: python3 -m astrid packs inspect <pack_id> [--agent] [--json]
    98	    """
    99	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
   100	        prog="python3 -m astrid packs inspect",
   101	        description="Show details for an installed pack.",
   102	    )
   103	    parser.add_argument(
   104	        "pack_id",
   105	        help="Pack identifier to inspect.",
   106	    )
   107	    parser.add_argument(
   108	        "--agent",
   109	        action="store_true",
   110	        help="Emit agent-focused subset (purpose, entrypoints, constraints, "
   111	        "context, secrets).",
   112	    )
   113	    parser.add_argument(
   114	        "--json",
   115	        action="store_true",
   116	        dest="json",
   117	        help="Output as JSON.",
   118	    )
   119	    parser.add_argument(
   120	        "--pack-root", action="append", dest="pack_roots",
   121	        help="Additional pack collection root (also honors ASTRID_PACKS_PATH).",
   122	    )
   123	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
   124	    return _inspect_installed_pack(
   125	        pack_id=args.pack_id,
   126	        agent=bool(args.agent),
   127	        json_output=bool(args.json),
   128	    )

   135	
   136	def _build_agent_view(manifest: dict, trust_summary: dict) -> dict:
   137	    """Build an agent-focused subset of a pack manifest."""
   138	    agent_section = manifest.get("agent", {}) if isinstance(manifest.get("agent"), dict) else {}
   139	    secrets_section = manifest.get("secrets")
   140	
   141	    view: dict = {}
   142	
   143	    # Purpose
   144	    purpose = agent_section.get("purpose")
   145	    if purpose:
   146	        view["purpose"] = str(purpose)
   147	
   148	    # Entrypoints — prefer normal_entrypoints, fall back to entrypoints
   149	    normal_entrypoints = trust_summary.get("normal_entrypoints", [])
   150	    if not normal_entrypoints and isinstance(agent_section.get("normal_entrypoints"), list):
   151	        normal_entrypoints = [str(ep) for ep in agent_section["normal_entrypoints"] if ep]
   152	    entrypoints = trust_summary.get("entrypoints", [])
   153	    if not entrypoints and isinstance(agent_section.get("entrypoints"), list):
   154	        entrypoints = [str(ep) for ep in agent_section["entrypoints"] if ep]
   155	    display_entrypoints = normal_entrypoints if normal_entrypoints else entrypoints
   156	    if display_entrypoints:
   157	        view["normal_entrypoints"] = normal_entrypoints if normal_entrypoints else None
   158	        view["entrypoints"] = display_entrypoints
   159	
   160	    # Constraints (from agent section or metadata)
   161	    constraints = agent_section.get("constraints")
   162	    if constraints is None:
   163	        metadata = manifest.get("metadata", {}) if isinstance(manifest.get("metadata"), dict) else {}
   164	        constraints = metadata.get("constraints")
   165	    if constraints:
   166	        view["constraints"] = constraints if isinstance(constraints, str) else str(constraints)
   167	
   168	    # Context (from agent section or metadata)
   169	    context = agent_section.get("context")
   170	    if context is None:
   171	        metadata = manifest.get("metadata", {}) if isinstance(manifest.get("metadata"), dict) else {}
   172	        context = metadata.get("context")
   173	    if context:
   174	        view["context"] = context if isinstance(context, str) else str(context)
   175	
   176	    # do_not_use_for and required_context from agent section
   177	    do_not_use_for = agent_section.get("do_not_use_for")
   178	    if do_not_use_for:
   179	        view["do_not_use_for"] = str(do_not_use_for)
   180	
   181	    required_context = agent_section.get("required_context")
   182	    if isinstance(required_context, list):
   183	        view["required_context"] = [str(rc) for rc in required_context if rc]
   184	
   185	    # Secrets — handle both new and old formats
   186	    if isinstance(secrets_section, list):
   187	        # New format: list of {name, required, description}
   188	        structured_secrets: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   189	        for s_obj in secrets_section:
   190	            if isinstance(s_obj, dict) and s_obj.get("name"):
   191	                structured_secrets.append({
   192	                    "name": str(s_obj["name"]),
   193	                    "required": bool(s_obj.get("required", False)),
   194	                    "description": str(s_obj.get("description", "")),
   195	                })
   196	        view["secrets"] = structured_secrets
   197	    elif isinstance(secrets_section, dict):
   198	        # Old format: dict with 'required' list
   199	        secrets_list: list[str] = trust_summary.get("declared_secrets", [])
   200	        if not secrets_list and isinstance(secrets_section.get("required"), list):
   201	            secrets_list = [str(s) for s in secrets_section["required"] if s]
   202	        if secrets_list:
   203	            view["secrets"] = secrets_list
   204	
   205	    # Keywords and capabilities from manifest
   206	    keywords_raw = manifest.get("keywords")
   207	    if isinstance(keywords_raw, list):
   208	        view["keywords"] = [str(k) for k in keywords_raw if k]
   209	
   210	    capabilities_raw = manifest.get("capabilities")
   211	    if isinstance(capabilities_raw, list):
   212	        view["capabilities"] = [str(c) for c in capabilities_raw if c]
   213	
   214	    # Permissions and trust metadata — sourced from extract_trust_summary()
   215	    permissions = trust_summary.get("permissions")
   216	    if permissions:
   217	        view["permissions"] = permissions
   218	    permission_ids = trust_summary.get("permission_ids")
   219	    if permission_ids:
   220	        view["permission_ids"] = permission_ids
   300	
   301	def _read_stage_excerpt(stage_path: Path, *, max_lines: int = 30) -> str | None:
   302	    """Return a bounded excerpt from a STAGE.md file.
   303	
   304	    Reads at most *max_lines* lines, stopping early at the first ``##``
   305	    heading (ATX level-2).  Returns ``None`` when the file cannot be read.
   306	    """
   307	    if not stage_path.is_file():
   308	        return None
   309	    try:
   310	        text = stage_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
   311	    except OSError:
   312	        return None
   313	    lines = text.splitlines()
   314	    excerpt_lines: list[str] = []
   315	    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
   316	        if i >= max_lines:
   317	            break
   318	        if line.startswith("##") and i > 0:
   319	            break
   320	        excerpt_lines.append(line)
   321	    return "\n".join(excerpt_lines).strip() or None
   322	
   323	
   324	def _scan_inspect_components(
   325	    rev_dir: Path | None, manifest: dict[str, Any]
   326	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   327	    """Scan component manifests under declared content roots in *rev_dir*.
   328	
   329	    Returns a deterministic (sorted by id) list of component overview dicts.
   330	    Each dict includes: id, name, kind, description, runtime, is_entrypoint,
   331	    docs_paths, stage_excerpt.
   332	    """
   333	    if rev_dir is None:
   334	        return []
   335	
   336	    content = manifest.get("content", {}) if isinstance(manifest.get("content"), dict) else {}
   337	    agent = manifest.get("agent", {}) if isinstance(manifest.get("agent"), dict) else {}
   338	    normal_eps = set()
   339	    if isinstance(agent.get("normal_entrypoints"), list):
   340	        normal_eps = {str(ep) for ep in agent["normal_entrypoints"] if ep}
   341	    if not normal_eps and isinstance(agent.get("entrypoints"), list):
   342	        normal_eps = {str(ep) for ep in agent["entrypoints"] if ep}
   343	
   344	    components: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   345	
   346	    for comp_kind in ("executors", "orchestrators"):
   347	        comp_root_rel = content.get(comp_kind)
   348	        if not isinstance(comp_root_rel, str) or not comp_root_rel.strip():
   349	            continue
   350	        comp_root = rev_dir / comp_root_rel
   351	        if not comp_root.is_dir():
   352	            continue
   353	
   354	        manifest_kind = comp_kind.rstrip("s")  # "executors" -> "executor"
   355	
   356	        for comp_dir in sorted(comp_root.iterdir()):
   357	            if not comp_dir.is_dir() or comp_dir.name.startswith("."):
   358	                continue
   359	            if comp_dir.name == "__pycache__":
   360	                continue
   361	
   362	            mf_path = _find_component_manifest(comp_dir, manifest_kind)
   363	            if mf_path is None:
   364	                continue
   365	
   366	            try:
   367	                data = load_manifest_mapping(mf_path, manifest_kind=manifest_kind)
   368	            except ManifestParseError:
   369	                continue
   370	
   371	            comp_id = str(data.get("id", comp_dir.name))
   372	            name = str(data.get("name", comp_id))
   373	            description = str(data.get("description", ""))
   374	            kind = str(data.get("kind", manifest_kind))
   375	
   376	            # Runtime
   377	            runtime_raw = data.get("runtime", {}) if isinstance(data.get("runtime"), dict) else {}
   378	            runtime: dict[str, Any] | None = None
   379	            if runtime_raw:
   380	                runtime = {
   381	                    "type": runtime_raw.get("type"),
   382	                    "entrypoint": runtime_raw.get("entrypoint"),
   383	                    "callable": runtime_raw.get("callable"),
   384	                }
   385	
   386	            # Is entrypoint?
   387	            is_entrypoint = comp_id in normal_eps
   388	
   389	            # Docs paths
   390	            docs = data.get("docs", {}) if isinstance(data.get("docs"), dict) else {}
   391	            stage_rel = docs.get("stage", "STAGE.md")
   392	            stage_path = comp_dir / stage_rel
   393	            docs_paths: dict[str, str] = {"stage": str(stage_path)}
   394	
   395	            # Stage excerpt
   396	            stage_excerpt = _read_stage_excerpt(stage_path)
   397	
   398	            components.append({
   399	                "id": comp_id,
   400	                "name": name,
   401	                "kind": kind,
   402	                "description": description,
   403	                "runtime": runtime,
   404	                "is_entrypoint": is_entrypoint,
   405	                "docs_paths": docs_paths,
   406	                "stage_excerpt": stage_excerpt,
   407	            })
   408	
   409	    # Elements: two-level structure — elements/<kind>/<element_name>/
   410	    elements_root_rel = content.get("elements")
   411	    if isinstance(elements_root_rel, str) and elements_root_rel.strip():
   412	        elements_root = rev_dir / elements_root_rel
   413	        if elements_root.is_dir():
   414	            for kind_dir in sorted(elements_root.iterdir()):
   415	                if not kind_dir.is_dir() or kind_dir.name.startswith("."):
   416	                    continue
   417	                if kind_dir.name == "__pycache__":
   418	                    continue
   419	
   420	                for elem_dir in sorted(kind_dir.iterdir()):
   421	                    if not elem_dir.is_dir() or elem_dir.name.startswith("."):
   422	                        continue
   423	                    if elem_dir.name == "__pycache__":
   424	                        continue
   425	
   426	                    mf_path = _find_component_manifest(elem_dir, "element")
   427	                    if mf_path is None:
   428	                        continue
   429	
   430	                    try:
   431	                        data = load_manifest_mapping(mf_path, manifest_kind="element")
   432	                    except ManifestParseError:
   433	                        continue
   434	
   435	                    comp_id = str(data.get("id", elem_dir.name))
   436	                    name = str(data.get("metadata", {}).get("label", comp_id)) if isinstance(data.get("metadata"), dict) else str(data.get("name", comp_id))
   437	                    description = str(data.get("description", ""))
   438	                    kind = str(data.get("kind", kind_dir.name.rstrip("s")))
   439	
   440	                    # Elements have no runtime/entrypoint
   441	                    runtime = None
   442	                    is_entrypoint = False
   443	
   444	                    # Docs paths
   445	                    docs = data.get("docs", {}) if isinstance(data.get("docs"), dict) else {}
   446	                    stage_rel = docs.get("stage", "STAGE.md")
   447	                    stage_path = elem_dir / stage_rel
   448	                    docs_paths: dict[str, str] = {"stage": str(stage_path)}
   449	
   450	                    # Stage excerpt
   451	                    stage_excerpt = _read_stage_excerpt(stage_path)
   452	
   453	                    components.append({
   454	                        "id": comp_id,
   455	                        "name": name,
   456	                        "kind": kind,
   457	                        "description": description,
   458	                        "runtime": runtime,
   459	                        "is_entrypoint": is_entrypoint,
   460	                        "docs_paths": docs_paths,
   461	                        "stage_excerpt": stage_excerpt,
   462	                    })
   463	
   464	    # Sort by id for determinism
   465	    components.sort(key=lambda c: c["id"])
   466	    return components
   467	
   468	
   469	def _build_full_inspect(
   470	    record: "InstallRecord", manifest: dict, trust_summary: dict,
   471	    *, rev_dir: "Path | None" = None,
   472	) -> dict:
   473	    """Build a full inspect dict for JSON or pretty-print output.
   474	
   475	    When *rev_dir* is provided, component manifests under declared content
   476	    roots are scanned and STAGE.md excerpts are extracted for each component.
   477	    """
   478	    # ── Structured secrets ──────────────────────────────────────────
   479	    secrets_raw = manifest.get("secrets")
   480	    structured_secrets: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   481	    if isinstance(secrets_raw, list):
   482	        for s_obj in secrets_raw:
   483	            if isinstance(s_obj, dict) and s_obj.get("name"):
   484	                structured_secrets.append({
   485	                    "name": str(s_obj["name"]),
   486	                    "required": bool(s_obj.get("required", False)),
   487	                    "description": str(s_obj.get("description", "")),
   488	                })
   489	    elif isinstance(secrets_raw, dict):
   490	        req_list = secrets_raw.get("required")
   491	        if isinstance(req_list, list):
   492	            for s in req_list:
   493	                if s:
   494	                    structured_secrets.append({
   495	                        "name": str(s), "required": True, "description": "",
   496	                    })
   497	
   498	    # ── Structured dependencies ─────────────────────────────────────
   499	    deps_raw = manifest.get("dependencies")
   500	    structured_deps: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
   501	    if isinstance(deps_raw, dict):
   502	        for eco in ("python", "npm", "system"):
   503	            eco_deps = deps_raw.get(eco)
   504	            if isinstance(eco_deps, list):
   505	                structured_deps[eco] = [str(d) for d in eco_deps if d]
   506	
   507	    # ── Components scan ─────────────────────────────────────────────
   508	    components = _scan_inspect_components(rev_dir, manifest) if rev_dir is not None else []
   509	    taxonomy = pack_taxonomy_from_manifest(manifest, status=str(manifest.get("status", "active")))
   510	
   511	    result = {
   512	        "pack_id": record.pack_id,
   513	        "name": record.name,
   514	        "version": record.version,
   515	        "schema_version": record.schema_version,
   516	        "description": manifest.get("description", ""),
   517	        "source_path": record.source_path,
   518	        "installed_at": record.installed_at,
   519	        "status": "active" if record.active else "inactive",
   520	        "component_counts": trust_summary.get("component_counts", {}),
   521	        "entrypoints": trust_summary.get("entrypoints", []),
   522	        "declared_secrets": trust_summary.get("declared_secrets", []),
   523	        "secrets": structured_secrets,  # structured: [{name, required, description}]
   524	        "dependencies": trust_summary.get("dependencies", []),
   525	        "dependencies_struct": trust_summary.get("dependencies_struct", {}),
   526	        "docs": trust_summary.get("docs", {}),
   527	        "warnings": trust_summary.get("warnings", []),
   528	        "agent": manifest.get("agent") if isinstance(manifest.get("agent"), dict) else None,
   529	        # Git-enriched and trust fields
   530	        "git_url": record.git_url,
   531	        "commit_sha": record.commit_sha,
   532	        "source_type": record.source_type,
   533	        "requested_ref": record.requested_ref,
   534	        "astrid_version": record.astrid_version if hasattr(record, 'astrid_version') else None,
   535	        "trust_tier": record.trust_tier,
   536	        "manifest_digest": record.manifest_digest if hasattr(record, 'manifest_digest') else None,
   537	        "previous_active_revision": record.previous_active_revision if hasattr(record, 'previous_active_revision') else None,
   538	        # New structured fields from trust_summary
   539	        "normal_entrypoints": trust_summary.get("normal_entrypoints", []),
   540	        "do_not_use_for": trust_summary.get("do_not_use_for"),
   541	        "required_context": trust_summary.get("required_context", []),
   542	        "keywords": trust_summary.get("keywords", []),
   543	        "capabilities": trust_summary.get("capabilities", []),
   544	        # Permissions and trust metadata — sourced from extract_trust_summary()
   545	        "permissions": trust_summary.get("permissions", []),
   546	        "permission_ids": trust_summary.get("permission_ids", []),
   547	        "trust": trust_summary.get("trust", {}),
   548	        **taxonomy,
   549	        "taxonomy": taxonomy,
   550	        # Component details (scanned from disk)
   551	        "components": components,
   552	    }
   553	    return result
   554	
   555	
   556	def _print_full_inspect(data: dict) -> None:
   557	    """Pretty-print a full pack inspect result."""
   558	    print(f"━━━ Pack: {data['pack_id']} ━━━")
   559	    print(f"  Name:          {data['name']}")
   560	    print(f"  Version:       {data['version']}")
   561	    print(f"  Schema:        {data['schema_version']}")
   562	    print(f"  Status:        {data['status']}")
   563	    print(f"  Source:        {data['source_path']}")
   564	    print(f"  Installed:     {data['installed_at']}")
   565	
   566	    desc = data.get("description")
   567	    if desc:
   568	        print(f"  Description:   {desc}")
   569	
   570	    _print_taxonomy_block(data.get("taxonomy", {}), indent="  ")
   571	
   572	    # Git-enriched fields
   573	    git_url = data.get("git_url", "")
   574	    if git_url:
   575	        print(f"  Git URL:       {git_url}")
   576	
   577	    commit_sha = data.get("commit_sha", "")
   578	    if commit_sha:
   579	        print(f"  Commit SHA:    {commit_sha[:8]}")
   580	
   581	    source_type = data.get("source_type", "")
   582	    if source_type:
   583	        print(f"  Source Type:   {source_type}")
   584	
   585	    requested_ref = data.get("requested_ref", "")
   586	    if requested_ref:
   587	        print(f"  Requested Ref: {requested_ref}")
   588	
   589	    astrid_version = data.get("astrid_version", "")
   590	    if astrid_version:
   591	        print(f"  Astrid Ver:    {astrid_version}")
   592

   594	    if trust_tier:

   596	
   597	    manifest_digest = data.get("manifest_digest", "")
   598	    if manifest_digest:
   599	        print(f"  Manifest Hash: {manifest_digest}")
   600	
   601	    previous = data.get("previous_active_revision", "")
   602	    if previous:
   603	        print(f"  Prev Revision: {previous}")
   604	
   605	    # Components
   606	    counts = data.get("component_counts", {})
   607	    if counts:
   608	        parts = []
   609	        for k in ("executors", "orchestrators", "elements"):
   610	            if counts.get(k, 0):
   611	                parts.append(f"{counts[k]} {k}")
   612	        if parts:
   613	            print(f"  Components:    {', '.join(parts)}")
   614	        else:
   615	            print("  Components:    (none)")
   616	    else:
   617	        print("  Components:    (none)")
   618	
   619	    # Entrypoints
   620	    entrypoints = data.get("entrypoints", [])
   621	    if entrypoints:
   622	        print(f"  Entrypoints:   {', '.join(entrypoints)}")
   623	
   624	    # Secrets (structured)
   625	    secrets = data.get("secrets", [])
   626	    if secrets:
   627	        if isinstance(secrets, list) and secrets and isinstance(secrets[0], dict):
   628	            for s_obj in secrets:
   629	                req = " (required)" if s_obj.get("required") else ""
   630	                desc = s_obj.get("description", "")
   631	                print(f"  Secret:        {s_obj['name']}{req}{': ' + desc if desc else ''}")
   632	        else:
   633	            print(f"  Secrets:       {', '.join(str(s) for s in secrets)}")
   634	
   635	    # Dependencies
   636	    deps = data.get("dependencies", [])

   721	                print(f"    • {p.get('id', '?')}: {reason}{svc_str}")

   740	def _inspect_discovered_pack(*, pack_id: str, agent: bool, json_output: bool, pack_roots: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> int:
   741	    """Render discovery-backed inspect output for non-installed packs."""
   742	    roots = [packs_root(), *[Path(item).expanduser() for item in pack_roots]]
   743	    roots.extend(
   744	        Path(item).expanduser()
   745	        for item in os.environ.get("ASTRID_PACKS_PATH", "").split(os.pathsep)
   746	        if item
   747	    )
   748	    packs: dict[str, PackDefinition] = {}
   749	    for root in roots:
   750	        for pack in discover_packs(root, include_hidden=True):
   751	            packs.setdefault(pack.id, pack)
   752	    pack = packs.get(pack_id)
   753	    if pack is None:
   754	        raise AstridError(
   755	            f"packs inspect: unknown pack {pack_id!r}",
   756	            recovery_command="List available packs: python3 -m astrid packs list",
   757	        )
   758	
   759	    payload = pack.agent if agent else _pack_payload(pack)
   760	    if json_output:
   761	        print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
   762	        return 0
   763	
   764	    if agent:
   765	        for key, value in sorted(payload.items()):
   766	            print(f"{key}: {value}")
   767	        return 0
   768	
   769	    for key in ("id", "name", "version", "description", "status", "visibility", "root", "manifest_path"):
   770	        print(f"{key}: {payload.get(key, '')}")
   771	    _print_taxonomy_block(payload.get("taxonomy", _pack_taxonomy(pack)))
   772	    if pack.content:
   773	        print("content:")
   774	        for key, value in sorted(pack.content.items()):
   775	            print(f"  {key}: {value}")
   776	    if pack.agent:
   777	        print("agent:")
   778	        for key, value in sorted(pack.agent.items()):
   779	            print(f"  {key}: {value}")
   780	    return 0

   783	def _handle_inspect(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
   784	    """Handler for ``packs inspect``."""
   785	    from astrid.core.pack.store import InstalledPackStore
   786	
   787	    store = InstalledPackStore()
   788	    if store.get_active(args.pack_id) is None:
   789	        return _inspect_discovered_pack(
   790	            pack_id=args.pack_id,
   791	            agent=bool(args.agent),
   792	            json_output=bool(args.json),
   793	            pack_roots=tuple(args.pack_roots or ()),
   794	        )
   795	
   796	    return _inspect_installed_pack(
   797	        pack_id=args.pack_id,
   798	        agent=bool(args.agent),
   799	        json_output=bool(args.json),
   800	    )
     1	"""Canonical entrypoint guard for pack run.py modules.
     2	
     3	Each pack's ``run.py`` ``__main__`` block should call
     4	``guard_canonical_entrypoint("<pack_id>")`` *before* any other logic. The
     5	guard refuses direct invocation (e.g. ``python -m astrid.packs.video_editing.orchestrators.hype.run``)
     6	and only allows the call to proceed when launched from the canonical Astrid
     7	runners, which set ``ASTRID_INTERNAL_INVOCATION=1`` in the subprocess env, or
     8	from the sanctioned in-process runtime context.
     9	"""
    10	
    11	from __future__ import annotations
    12	
    13	from contextlib import contextmanager
    14	from contextvars import ContextVar
    15	from typing import Callable, Iterator
    16	
    17	from astrid.core.contracts.errors import AstridError, render_astrid_error, wrap_degraded_error
    18	from astrid.core.env_vars import ASTRID_INTERNAL_INVOCATION, ASTRID_PROJECT_RUN
    19	
    20	_CANONICAL_RUNTIME_CAPABILITY: ContextVar[str | None] = ContextVar(
    21	    "astrid_canonical_runtime_capability",
    22	    default=None,
    23	)
    24	
    25	
    26	@contextmanager
    27	def canonical_runtime_entrypoint(capability_id: str) -> Iterator[None]:
    28	    """Allow guarded imports/execution for one capability in this call stack."""
    29	
    30	    token = _CANONICAL_RUNTIME_CAPABILITY.set(capability_id)
    31	    try:
    32	        yield
    33	    finally:
    34	        _CANONICAL_RUNTIME_CAPABILITY.reset(token)
    35	
    36	
    37	def guard_canonical_entrypoint(pack_id: str) -> None:
    38	    """Refuse direct invocation. Call from each pack's ``__main__`` block."""
    39	    import os
    40	    import sys
    41	
    42	    if os.environ.get(ASTRID_INTERNAL_INVOCATION):
    43	        return
    44	    if _CANONICAL_RUNTIME_CAPABILITY.get() == pack_id:
    45	        return
    46	    print(
    47	        f"error: this pack ({pack_id}) is not meant to be invoked directly; "
    48	        f"run `astrid --help`, `astrid doctor`, or use the SDK "
    49	        f"(astrid.sdk.invoke) instead.\n"
    50	        f"(direct `python -m astrid.packs.<...>.run` invocation is reserved\n"
    51	        f"for internal use by the astrid runner.)",
    52	        file=sys.stderr,
    53	    )
    54	    sys.exit(2)
    55	
    56	
    57	def warn_if_unledgered() -> None:
    58	    """Emit a stderr warning when a generation executor's main() runs without the
    59	    harness marker ``ASTRID_PROJECT_RUN``.
    60	
    61	    This is warning-only — no ledger entry is created.  When the environment
    62	    variable is present the call is in-band and no warning is produced.
    63	    """
    64	    import os
    65	    import sys
    66	
    67	    if not os.environ.get(ASTRID_PROJECT_RUN):
    68	        print(
    69	            "[astrid] running unledgered — invoke through executors run"
    70	            " or the SDK to persist a run record",
    71	            file=sys.stderr,
    72	        )
    73	
    74	
    75	def run_pack_main(
    76	    capability_id: str,
    77	    runner: Callable[[], int],
    78	    *,
    79	    argv: list[str] | None = None,
    80	    recovery_command: str | None = None,
    81	) -> int:
    82	    """Run a pack entrypoint with AstridError rendering and degraded fallback."""
    83	
    84	    snapshot = {"argv": list(argv or ()), "capability_id": capability_id}
    85	    try:
    86	        return runner()
    87	    except AstridError as exc:
    88	        return render_astrid_error(exc)
    89	    except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
    90	        return render_astrid_error(
    91	            AstridError(
    92	                str(exc),
    93	                recovery_command=recovery_command or f"python3 -m astrid executors run {capability_id} --help",
    94	                state_snapshot=snapshot,
    95	            )
    96	        )
    97	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
    98	        bug = wrap_degraded_error(
    99	            exc,
   100	            state_snapshot=snapshot,

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	set -euo pipefail
     3	
     4	# Build one wheel and run the small installed-product smoke through the shared
     5	# artifact harness.  The harness owns wheel selection, identity, isolation,
     6	# credential scrubbing, lane evidence, and cleanup; this wrapper only chooses
     7	# the smoke lanes and reports their results.
     8	
     9	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    10	PYTHON_BIN="${PYTHON_BIN:-python3}"
    11	EXPLICIT_WORKSPACE="${SMOKE_WHEEL_WORKSPACE:-}"
    12	
    13	cd "$REPO_ROOT"
    14	
    15	if [[ -n "$EXPLICIT_WORKSPACE" ]]; then
    16	  WORKSPACE_ARGS=("--workspace" "$EXPLICIT_WORKSPACE")
    17	else
    18	  WORKSPACE_ARGS=()
    19	fi
    20	
    21	exec "$PYTHON_BIN" - "$REPO_ROOT" "${WORKSPACE_ARGS[@]}" <<'PY'
    22	from __future__ import annotations
    23	
    24	import json
    25	import sys
    26	from importlib import resources
    27	from pathlib import Path
    28	
    29	repo_root = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
    30	sys.path.insert(0, str(repo_root))
    31	
    32	from scripts.reshape.installed_artifact import build_once
    33	
    34	
    35	args = sys.argv[2:]
    36	workspace = None
    37	if args:
    38	    if len(args) != 2 or args[0] != "--workspace":
    39	        raise SystemExit(f"invalid workspace arguments: {args!r}")
    40	    workspace = Path(args[1]).expanduser().resolve()
    41	
    42	print("=== installed Astrid wheel smoke ===")
    43	print(f"repository: {repo_root}")
    44	if workspace is not None:
    45	    print(f"workspace: {workspace}")
    46	
    47	harness = build_once(
    48	    repo_root,
    49	    workspace=workspace,
    50	    # The smoke is a user-facing product check, so install the wheel with its
    51	    # declared runtime dependencies.  T3's no-dependency harness remains the
    52	    # stricter dependency-leak proof.
    53	    install_dependencies=True,
    54	)
    55	owned_workspace = workspace is None
    56	workspace_path = harness.workspace
    57	try:
    58	    version = harness.run_module("version", "astrid", ["--version"], check=True)
    59	    assert version.stdout.strip() == "astrid", version.stdout
    60	
    61	    help_record = harness.run_module("help", "astrid", ["help"], check=True)
    62	    assert "Family census (exactly eight families):" in help_record.stdout
    63	    assert "timelines shots       [pack: shots]" in help_record.stdout
    64	    assert "media references      [pack: references]" in help_record.stdout
    65	
    66	    # ``doctor --json`` is intentionally run against the fresh isolated
    67	    # workspace.  A clean workspace has no database yet, so either a healthy
    68	    # result (if a caller pre-seeded it) or doctor’s documented fail-closed
    69	    # result is valid; import/parse failures are not.
    70	    doctor = harness.run_module("doctor", "astrid", ["doctor", "--json"])
    71	    if doctor.returncode not in (0, 1):
    72	        raise RuntimeError(doctor.error or doctor.output)
    73	    doctor_payload = json.loads(doctor.stdout)
    74	    assert isinstance(doctor_payload.get("checks"), list)
    75	    assert isinstance(doctor_payload.get("ok"), bool)
    76	
    77	    resource_probe = harness.run_lane(
    78	        "resources",
    79	        [
    80	            "-c",
    81	            "from importlib import resources; "
    82	            "required=('core/migrations/sql/core/0001_initial.sql',"
    83	            "'packs/timeline/schema-pack.yaml','packs/shots/schema-pack.yaml',"
    84	            "'packs/references/schema-pack.yaml'); "
    85	            "root=resources.files('astrid'); "
    86	            "missing=[name for name in required if not root.joinpath(*name.split('/')).is_file()]; "
    87	            "assert not missing, missing; print('package resources: OK')",
    88	        ],
    89	        check=True,
    90	    )
    91	    assert "package resources: OK" in resource_probe.stdout
    92	
    93	    # Adversarial lanes prove that a missing resource and a checkout import
    94	    # cannot be mistaken for a passing installed-artifact result.
    95	    missing = harness.run_lane(
    96	        "missing-resource",
    97	        [
    98	            "-c",
    99	            "from importlib import resources; "
   100	            "assert resources.files('astrid').joinpath('not-shipped.txt').is_file()",
   101	        ],
   102	    )
   103	    if missing.returncode == 0 or missing.status != "failed":
   104	        raise RuntimeError(f"missing-resource adversary unexpectedly passed: {missing.as_dict()}")
   105	
   106	    checkout = harness.run_lane(
   107	        "checkout-import",
   108	        ["-c", f"print({str(repo_root)!r})"],
   109	    )
   110	    if checkout.returncode != 0 or checkout.status != "failed":
   111	        raise RuntimeError(f"checkout-import adversary was not rejected: {checkout.as_dict()}")
   112	    if not checkout.error or "source-tree path" not in checkout.error:
   113	        raise RuntimeError(f"checkout-import failure lacked source evidence: {checkout.as_dict()}")
   114	
   115	    print(json.dumps({
   116	        "schema": "astrid.installed_smoke.v1",
   117	        "wheel_sha256": harness.artifact_digest,
   118	        "version": harness.installed_version,
   119	        "doctor_ok": doctor_payload["ok"],
   120	        "resource_lane": resource_probe.as_dict(),
   121	        "missing_resource_lane": missing.as_dict(),
   122	        "checkout_import_lane": checkout.as_dict(),
   123	    }, sort_keys=True))
   124	finally:
   125	    harness.close()
   126	
   127	if owned_workspace:
   128	    if workspace_path.exists():
   129	        raise RuntimeError(f"owned harness workspace was not cleaned: {workspace_path}")
   130	else:
   131	    if not workspace_path.is_dir():
   132	        raise RuntimeError(f"explicit harness workspace was not preserved: {workspace_path}")
   133	
   134	print("=== installed Astrid wheel smoke PASSED ===")

    77	def _snapshot_ignore(_directory: str, names: list[str]) -> set[str]:
    78	    ignored = {
    79	        ".git",
    80	        ".megaplan",
    81	        ".pytest_cache",
    82	        ".mypy_cache",
    83	        ".ruff_cache",
    84	        "__pycache__",
    85	        "build",
    86	        "dist",
    87	        "out",
    88	        "runs",
    89	        "projects",
    90	        "node_modules",
    91	        ".venv",
    92	        "venv",
    93	        "astrid.egg-info",
    94	    }
    95	    return {name for name in names if name in ignored or name.endswith(".egg-info")}

    98	@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
    99	def wheel(tmp_path_factory: pytest.TempPathFactory) -> Path:
   100	    root = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("m8-packaging")
   101	    source = root / "source"
   102	    shutil.copytree(REPO_ROOT, source, ignore=_snapshot_ignore)
   103	    dist = root / "dist"
   104	    dist.mkdir()
   105	    result = subprocess.run(
   106	        [sys.executable, "-m", "build", "--wheel", "--outdir", str(dist)],
   107	        cwd=source,
   108	        capture_output=True,
   109	        text=True,
   110	        check=False,
   111	    )
   112	    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stdout + result.stderr
   113	    wheels = sorted(dist.glob("*.whl"))
   114	    assert len(wheels) == 1, [path.name for path in wheels]
   115	    return wheels[0]

   118	@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
   119	def installed(wheel: Path, tmp_path_factory: pytest.TempPathFactory) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
   120	    root = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("m8-installed")
   121	    venv = root / "venv"
   122	    result = subprocess.run(
   123	        # T2 is the wheel-content/entry-point contract.  The shared T3
   124	        # harness owns the stricter no-system-site-packages dependency-leak
   125	        # proof; using the already provisioned test dependencies here keeps
   126	        # this package contract deterministic in an offline checkout.
   127	        [sys.executable, "-m", "venv", "--system-site-packages", str(venv)],
   128	        capture_output=True,
   129	        text=True,
   130	        check=False,
   131	    )
   132	    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stdout + result.stderr
   133	    child_python = venv / "bin" / "python"
   134	    result = subprocess.run(
   135	        [
   136	            str(child_python),
   137	            "-m",
   138	            "pip",
   139	            "install",
   140	            "--disable-pip-version-check",
   141	            "--no-input",
   142	            "--no-deps",
   143	            "--no-index",
   144	            str(wheel),
   145	        ],
   146	        capture_output=True,
   147	        text=True,
   148	        check=False,
   149	    )
   150	    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stdout + result.stderr
   151	    outside = root / "outside-checkout"
   152	    outside.mkdir()
   153	    env = {
   154	        "PATH": os.environ.get("PATH", os.defpath),
   155	        "HOME": str(root / "home"),
   156	        "ASTRID_HOME": str(root / "state"),
   157	        "ASTRID_PROJECTS_ROOT": str(root / "projects"),
   158	        "XDG_CACHE_HOME": str(root / "cache"),
   159	        "XDG_CONFIG_HOME": str(root / "config"),
   160	        "PYTHONNOUSERSITE": "1",
   161	        "PYTHONSAFEPATH": "1",
   162	    }
   163	    for value in env.values():
   164	        if value.startswith(str(root)):
   165	            Path(value).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   166	    return child_python, outside

   168	
   169	def _run_installed(
   170	    installed: tuple[Path, Path], args: list[str], *, env: dict[str, str] | None = None
   171	) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
   172	    child_python, outside = installed
   173	    child_env = os.environ.copy()
   174	    child_env.update(env or {})
   175	    child_env.pop("PYTHONPATH", None)
   176	    child_env.pop("PYTHONHOME", None)
   177	    return subprocess.run(
   178	        # This T2 fixture intentionally reuses the already-provisioned global
   179	        # runtime dependencies through --system-site-packages. T3 owns the
   180	        # stricter no-system-site-packages dependency-leak proof; PYTHONNOUSERSITE
   181	        # and PYTHONSAFEPATH still keep user/site and checkout paths out.
   182	        [str(child_python), *args],
   183	        cwd=outside,
   184	        env=child_env,
   185	        capture_output=True,
   186	        text=True,
   187	        check=False,
   188	    )

   191	def test_wheel_metadata_entry_points_and_runtime_modules(wheel: Path) -> None:
   192	    with zipfile.ZipFile(wheel) as archive:
   193	        names = set(archive.namelist())
   194	        metadata_path = next(name for name in names if name.endswith(".dist-info/METADATA"))
   195	        metadata = email.message_from_bytes(archive.read(metadata_path))
   196	        entry_points_path = next(name for name in names if name.endswith(".dist-info/entry_points.txt"))
   197	        entry_points = archive.read(entry_points_path).decode("utf-8")
   198	
   199	    assert metadata["Name"] == "astrid"
   200	    assert metadata["Version"] == "0.1.0"
   201	    assert metadata["Requires-Python"] == ">=3.11"
   202	    assert "astrid = astrid.core.gateway:main" in entry_points
   203	    assert EXPECTED_RUNTIME_MODULES <= names
   204	    assert EXPECTED_RESOURCES <= names

   276	def _too_new_database(path: Path, pack: str) -> None:
   277	    connection = sqlite3.connect(path)
   278	    try:
   279	        connection.execute(
   280	            "CREATE TABLE schema_migrations (pack TEXT, version INTEGER, name TEXT, checksum TEXT, applied_at TEXT)"
   281	        )
   282	        connection.execute(
   283	            "INSERT INTO schema_migrations VALUES (?, ?, 'future', 'future', 'future')", (pack, 99)
   284	        )
   285	        connection.commit()
   286	    finally:
   287	        connection.close()
   288

   290	@pytest.mark.parametrize("pack", ["core", "timeline"])
   291	def test_too_new_core_and_pack_migrations_refuse_without_mutation(
   292	    tmp_path: Path,
   293	    pack: str,
   294	) -> None:
   295	    database = tmp_path / f"{pack}.sqlite3"
   296	    _too_new_database(database, pack)
   297	    before = database.read_bytes()
   298	    with pytest.raises(MigrationTooNewError):
   299	        probe_database(database, build_standard_registry())
   300	    assert database.read_bytes() == before

   303	def test_shared_harness_smoke_checks_installed_basics_and_failure_boundaries(
   304	    tmp_path: Path,
   305	) -> None:
   306	    """Exercise the shared artifact boundary used by the release smoke.
   307	
   308	    The packaging fixture above intentionally retains its small T2-specific
   309	    setup.  This test covers the T4 contract: all product checks run through
   310	    the build-once harness, explicit workspaces survive close, and failed
   311	    resource/import probes remain nonzero evidence rather than being hidden.
   312	    """
   313	    workspace = tmp_path / "explicit-installed-workspace"
   314	    harness = build_once(
   315	        REPO_ROOT,
   316	        workspace=workspace,
   317	        # Help and doctor are gateway-level product checks and therefore need
   318	        # the wheel's declared runtime dependencies.  The T3 harness tests
   319	        # retain the no-dependency isolation proof separately.
   320	        install_dependencies=True,
   321	    )
   322	    try:
   323	        version = harness.run_module(
   324	            "installed-version", "astrid", ["--version"], check=True
   325	        )
   326	        assert version.stdout.strip() == "astrid"
   327	
   328	        help_record = harness.run_module("installed-help", "astrid", ["help"], check=True)
   329	        assert "Family census (exactly eight families):" in help_record.stdout
   330	
   331	        doctor_help = harness.run_module(
   332	            "installed-doctor-help", "astrid", ["doctor", "--help"], check=True
   333	        )
   334	        assert "doctor" in doctor_help.output.lower()
   335	
   336	        resources = harness.run_lane(
   337	            "installed-resource-probe",
   338	            [
   339	                "-c",
   340	                "from importlib import resources; "
   341	                "required=('core/migrations/sql/core/0001_initial.sql',"
   342	                "'packs/timeline/schema-pack.yaml','packs/shots/schema-pack.yaml',"
   343	                "'packs/references/schema-pack.yaml'); "
   344	                "root=resources.files('astrid'); "
   345	                "missing=[name for name in required if not root.joinpath(*name.split('/')).is_file()]; "
   346	                "assert not missing, missing; print('resources: OK')",
   347	            ],
   348	            check=True,
   349	        )
   350	        assert "resources: OK" in resources.stdout
   351	
   352	        missing = harness.run_lane(
   353	            "missing-resource-adversary",
   354	            [
   355	                "-c",
   356	                "from importlib import resources; "
   357	                "assert resources.files('astrid').joinpath('missing-release-resource').is_file()",
   358	            ],
   359	        )
   360	        assert missing.returncode != 0
   361	        assert missing.status == "failed"
   362	        assert missing.error and "status" in missing.error
   363	
   364	        checkout = harness.run_lane(
   365	            "checkout-import-adversary",
   366	            ["-c", f"print({str(REPO_ROOT)!r})"],
   367	        )

   369	        assert checkout.status == "failed"
   370	        assert checkout.error and "source-tree path" in checkout.error
   371	    finally:
   372	        harness.close()

   375	    # inspectable after the lane finishes.

   377	    assert (workspace / "dist").is_dir()

     1	"""Deterministic kernel application composition (m4 plan step 4, task T4).
     2	
     3	This module is the shared application boundary the SDK services and the
     4	bridge consume (SDK contract ``docs/contracts/astrid-sdk-v10.md`` section
     5	6). It composes, **explicitly and deterministically**:
     6	
     7	- exactly **one** :class:`~astrid.core.store.writer.DatabaseWriter` — the
     8	  single write queue every repository submits through;
     9	- the kernel repositories (projects, tasks, media, runs, evidence) and the
    10	  kernel services (event append, receipts);
    11	- a **read-only ordered** :class:`~astrid.core.repositories.EventRepository`
    12	  over the same writer for ordered event reads;
    13	- for the standard composition, the three explicitly registered in-tree
    14	  pack repositories (timeline, shots, references);
    15	- for the standard composition, all seven typed SDK services (projects,
    16	  timelines, media, tasks, runs, references, shots) over those shared
    17	  repositories — every service resolves through the application, holds no
    18	  SQL, and never opens a writer of its own.
    19	
    20	Rules enforced here:
    21	
    22	- **No tables are added.** The composition only opens the database through
    23	  the frozen migration catalog; the event repository issues ``SELECT``
    24	  only.
    25	- **No dynamic discovery.** Every repository and service is imported and
    26	  constructed by name; there is no module scanning, no pack loader, and no
    27	  install/uninstall path.
    28	- **Pack-independent core.** :func:`compose_core_application` never
    29	  imports ``astrid.packs``; the kernel repositories and the event
    30	  repository compose without any pack. The seven typed services are wired
    31	  only by the standard composition (Step 17), because the timeline service
    32	  consumes the timeline pack repository.
    33	- **Deterministic close.** :meth:`CoreApplication.close` drains the writer
    34	  queue, stops the writer thread, and closes the owned connection
    35	  (idempotent); the standard composition also closes the writer if any
    36	  wiring step fails mid-construction.
    37	
    38	- **Exclusive-owner lock (SD3-m4).** :func:`compose_standard_application`
    39	  acquires a process-lifetime :class:`astrid.core.store.ownership.DatabaseOwnerLock`
    40	  beside the database **before** opening the writer (so no second writable
    41	  connection or queue can open), and releases it on every close path. A
    42	  second owner fails closed with the SDK's typed ``unavailable`` contract
    43	  instead of leaking an OS or database error.
    44	
    45	Startup staging GC remains the serve composition root's concern
    46	(``compose_standard_bridge``).
    47	"""

   103	    and CLI timeline saves must all be observable here, over the one

   113	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
   114	class CoreApplication:
   115	    """Kernel-only application over exactly one writer queue.
   116	
   117	    Pack-independent: this composition contains no pack repository and the
   118	    wiring function that builds it never imports ``astrid.packs``. All
   119	    repositories share the single :attr:`writer`; :attr:`event_log`
   120	    provides read-only ordered event reads over the same writer.
   121	    """
   122	
   123	    projects_root: Path
   124	    registry: FrozenSchemaPackRegistry
   125	    writer: DatabaseWriter
   126	    events: EventAppendService
   127	    receipts: ReceiptService
   128	    projects: ProjectRepository
   129	    tasks: TaskRepository
   130	    media: MediaRepository
   131	    runs: RunRepository
   132	    evidence: EvidenceRepository
   133	    event_log: EventRepository
   134	    owner_lock: DatabaseOwnerLock | None
   135	
   136	    @property
   137	    def database_path(self) -> Path:
   138	        """The managed database path for this projects root (decision §5)."""
   139	        return derive_database_path(self.projects_root)
   140	
   141	    def close(self) -> None:
   142	        """Drain the writer queue, stop the writer thread, close the database.
   143	
   144	        Deterministic and idempotent: queued callbacks still execute, the
   145	        owned connection is closed by the writer thread itself, and a
   146	        second ``close()`` is a no-op (``DatabaseWriter.close`` contract).
   147	        When the composition holds the exclusive-owner lock (the standard
   148	        composition), it is released only after the writer is closed, so a
   149	        second owner can never acquire the database while this process
   150	        still holds an open writer.
   151	        """
   152	        self.writer.close()
   153	        if self.owner_lock is not None:
   154	            self.owner_lock.release()
   155	
   156	    def __enter__(self) -> Self:
   157	        return self
   158	
   159	    def __exit__(self, *exc_info: object) -> None:
   160	        self.close()
   161

   163	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
   164	class StandardApplication(CoreApplication):
   165	    """Standard-Astrid application: kernel plus packs plus typed services.
   166	
   167	    Extends :class:`CoreApplication` with the three explicitly registered
   168	    pack repositories (timeline, shots, references) and the seven typed SDK
   169	    services (projects, timelines, media, tasks, runs, references, shots),
   170	    all sharing the same single writer queue, registry, kernel services,
   171	    and read-only ordered event repository. The services hold no SQL and
   172	    never open a writer of their own — each one opens a
   173	    :class:`~astrid.core.store.uow.UnitOfWork` over the shared
   174	    :attr:`~CoreApplication.writer` per mutation.
   175	
   176	    Plan step 30 instruments exactly one service command —
   177	    :attr:`timelines_service` ``save`` — so every bridge, SDK, or CLI
   178	    timeline save is recorded in :attr:`timeline_save_calls` before it
   179	    commits through the one writer queue (the shared service-authority
   180	    proof's single instrumentation point).
   181	    """
   182	
   183	    timelines: TimelineRepository
   184	    shots: ShotRepository
   185	    references: ReferenceRepository
   186	    projects_service: ProjectsService
   187	    timelines_service: TimelinesService
   188	    media_service: MediaService
   189	    tasks_service: TasksService
   190	    runs_service: RunsService
   191	    references_service: ReferencesService
   192	    shots_service: ShotsService
   193	    # The shared service-authority instrumentation (plan step 30): every
   194	    # timeline save that crosses the application's single timeline service
   195	    # — from the bridge, the SDK, or the CLI — is recorded here, so tests
   196	    # can prove all three surfaces reach the same service command over the
   197	    # one writer queue with equivalent committed receipts.
   198	    timeline_save_calls: list[TimelineSaveCall]
   199	
   200	
   201	def compose_core_application(
   202	    writer: DatabaseWriter,
   203	    *,
   204	    registry: FrozenSchemaPackRegistry,
   205	    projects_root: str | Path,
   206	) -> CoreApplication:
   207	    """Wire the kernel-only application over one already-open writer.
   208	
   209	    The caller supplies the single writer (constructed through a store
   210	    seam such as the standard writer opener, or directly in tests)
   211	    together with the registry that writer's database was opened with and
   212	    the managed projects root. This function adds no tables, performs no
   213	    dynamic discovery, and never imports a pack, so the core composition
   214	    stays pack-independent.
   215	    """
   216	    root = Path(projects_root)
   217	    events = EventAppendService(registry)
   218	    receipts = ReceiptService()
   219	    projects = ProjectRepository(events=events, receipts=receipts)
   220	    tasks = TaskRepository(events=events, receipts=receipts)
   221	    media = MediaRepository(events=events, receipts=receipts, projects_root=root)
   222	    runs = RunRepository(events=events, receipts=receipts)
   223	    evidence = EvidenceRepository(events=events, receipts=receipts)
   224	    return CoreApplication(
   225	        projects_root=root,
   226	        registry=registry,
   227	        writer=writer,
   228	        events=events,
   229	        receipts=receipts,
   230	        projects=projects,
   231	        tasks=tasks,
   232	        media=media,
   233	        runs=runs,
   234	        evidence=evidence,
   235	        event_log=EventRepository(writer),
   236	        owner_lock=None,
   237	    )

   240	def _instrument_timeline_save(service: TimelinesService) -> list[TimelineSaveCall]:
   241	    """Install the one shared-service instrumentation point (plan step 30).
   242	
   243	    Wraps the application's single timeline service ``save`` command so
   244	    every bridge, SDK, or CLI timeline save is recorded once — before
   245	    delegating to the original command — into the returned list (exposed
   246	    as ``StandardApplication.timeline_save_calls``). The wrapper is
   247	    installed exactly once per standard application and is safe for
   248	    concurrent callers (the bridge serves requests on its own thread), so
   249	    the recorded calls prove that all three surfaces resolve to the same
   250	    service command over the one writer queue.
   251	    """
   252	    calls: list[TimelineSaveCall] = []
   253	    lock = threading.Lock()
   254	    original = service.save
   255	
   256	    def recorded(
   257	        project: str,
   258	        ref: str,
   259	        *,
   260	        config: Mapping[str, Any],
   261	        registry: Mapping[str, Any],
   262	        expected_version: int,
   263	        idempotency_key: str | None = None,
   264	    ) -> DomainResult[dict[str, Any]]:
   265	        with lock:
   266	            calls.append(
   267	                TimelineSaveCall(
   268	                    project=project,
   269	                    ref=ref,
   270	                    idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
   271	                    expected_version=expected_version,
   272	                )
   273	            )
   274	        return original(
   275	            project,
   276	            ref,
   277	            config=config,
   278	            registry=registry,
   279	            expected_version=expected_version,
   280	            idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
   281	        )
   282	
   283	    service.save = recorded  # type: ignore[method-assign]
   284	    return calls
