   287	def compose_standard_application(
   288	    projects_root: str | Path | None = None,
   289	    *,
   290	    registry: FrozenSchemaPackRegistry | None = None,
   291	    database_path: str | Path | None = None,
   292	) -> StandardApplication:
   293	    """Compose the standard application: one writer, kernel + pack repos.
   294	
   295	    Resolves the projects root (argument, ``ASTRID_PROJECTS_ROOT``, or the
   296	    default), derives ``${root}/.astrid/astrid.sqlite3`` (unless a
   297	    ``database_path`` is supplied), composes the standard registry (core +
   298	    exactly timeline, shots, references) unless one is injected, acquires
   299	    the exclusive-owner lock beside the database **before** opening the
   300	    writer, opens exactly one ``DatabaseWriter`` through the standard writer
   301	    seam, and wires every kernel and pack repository plus the read-only
   302	    ordered event repository. If any wiring step fails, the writer is closed
   303	    and the lock is released before the exception propagates, so composition
   304	    never leaks an open writer or a held owner lock. A second owner (another
   305	    process, or another composition in this process) fails closed with the
   306	    SDK's typed ``unavailable`` error.
   307	    """
   308	    root = resolve_projects_root(projects_root)
   309	    db_path = (
   310	        Path(database_path)
   311	        if database_path is not None
   312	        else derive_database_path(root)
   313	    )
   314	    db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   315	    if registry is None:
   316	        registry = build_standard_registry()
   317	    # Acquire the exclusive-owner lock before any writable connection or
   318	    # writer queue can open (SD3-m4). A second owner fails closed with the
   319	    # typed unavailable contract instead of leaking an OS/database error.
   320	    try:
   321	        owner_lock = DatabaseOwnerLock(db_path)
   322	    except OwnerLockError as exc:
   323	        raise ServiceUnavailableError(
   324	            "the canonical store is owned by another Astrid process. When "
   325	            "astrid serve is running, its bridge owns the store: use GET "
   326	            "/routes and its HTTP routes while it is running, or wait for a "
   327	            "clean shutdown. "
   328	            "Reads may retry after release. For writes, preserve the exact "
   329	            "payload and idempotency key, retry after release, and verify "
   330	            "state.",
   331	            details={
   332	                "reason": "store_owned",
   333	                "retryable": True,
   334	            },
   335	        ) from exc
   336	    writer: DatabaseWriter | None = None
   337	    try:
   338	        writer = open_standard_writer(db_path, registry=registry)
   339	        events = EventAppendService(registry)
   340	        receipts = ReceiptService()
   341	        projects = ProjectRepository(events=events, receipts=receipts)
   342	        timelines = TimelineRepository(
   343	            events=events, receipts=receipts, projects=projects
   344	        )
   345	        shots = ShotRepository(events=events, receipts=receipts)
   346	        references = ReferenceRepository(events=events, receipts=receipts)
   347	        tasks = TaskRepository(events=events, receipts=receipts)
   348	        media = MediaRepository(
   349	            events=events, receipts=receipts, projects_root=root
   350	        )
   351	        runs = RunRepository(events=events, receipts=receipts)
   352	        evidence = EvidenceRepository(events=events, receipts=receipts)
   353	        event_log = EventRepository(writer)
   354	        # The seven typed services, wired over the shared repositories and
   355	        # the single writer queue. Services contain no SQL and never open a
   356	        # writer of their own (plan step 17).
   357	        projects_service = ProjectsService(
   358	            writer, projects, receipts, projects_root=root
   359	        )
   360	        timelines_service = TimelinesService(
   361	            writer, projects, timelines, receipts
   362	        )
   363	        # One shared service-authority instrumentation point (plan step 30):
   364	        # every timeline save — bridge, SDK, or CLI — is recorded on the
   365	        # single timeline service before it commits through the one writer.
   366	        timeline_save_calls = _instrument_timeline_save(timelines_service)
   367	        media_service = MediaService(writer, projects, media, receipts)
   368	        runs_service = RunsService(
   369	            writer,
   370	            projects,
   371	            runs,
   372	            receipts,
   373	            evidence,
   374	            event_log,
   375	            tasks=tasks,
   376	            media=media,
   377	            projects_root=str(root),
   378	            registry=registry,
   379	        )
   380	        tasks_service = TasksService(
   381	            writer,
   382	            projects,
   383	            tasks,
   384	            receipts,
   385	            event_log,
   386	            media=media,
   387	            projects_root=str(root),
   388	            runs=runs_service,
   389	            registry=registry,
   390	        )
   391	        references_service = ReferencesService(
   392	            writer, projects, references, receipts
   393	        )
   394	        shots_service = ShotsService(writer, projects, shots, receipts, media)
   395	        return StandardApplication(
   396	            projects_root=root,
   397	            registry=registry,
   398	            writer=writer,
   399	            events=events,
   400	            receipts=receipts,
   401	            projects=projects,
   402	            timelines=timelines,
   403	            shots=shots,
   404	            references=references,
   405	            tasks=tasks,
   406	            media=media,
   407	            runs=runs,
   408	            evidence=evidence,
   409	            event_log=event_log,
   410	            owner_lock=owner_lock,
   150	    @property
   151	    def tasks(self) -> TasksService:
   152	        """Typed task service (create/list/show/cancel/retry/...)."""
   153	        return self._app.tasks_service

   199	    def invoke(self, capability_id: str, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
   200	        """Lazy typed ``astrid.sdk.invoke`` bound to the client's root.

   833	def _resolve_projects_root(project_root: str | Path | None, project: str | None) -> Path:
   834	    from astrid.core.foundation.project_paths import resolve_projects_root
   835	    if project_root is not None:
   836	        return Path(project_root).expanduser().resolve()
   837	    try:
   838	        return resolve_projects_root(None)
   839	    except Exception:
   840	        return Path.cwd().expanduser().resolve()

   842	def _kernel_invoke(
   843	    capability: Any,
   844	    *,
   845	    kind: Any,
   846	    project: str | None,
   847	    projects_root: Path,
   848	    inputs: Mapping[str, Any] | None,
   849	    outputs: Mapping[str, Any] | None,
   850	    extra_pack_roots: tuple[str, ...] = (),
   851	    idempotency_context: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
   852	    registry: FrozenSchemaPackRegistry | None = None,
   853	) -> tuple[str, str, str, Path | None, dict[str, Any], bool, Any]:
   854	    """Real kernel admission: RunRepository.create with compute_spec_hash idempotency, claim/start, handler, execute/complete."""
   855	    from astrid.core.repositories.tasks import compute_spec_hash
   856	    from astrid.core.store.uow import UnitOfWork
   857	    from astrid.core.store.writer import DatabaseWriter
   858	    from astrid.core.events.service import EventAppendService
   859	    from astrid.core.receipts.service import ReceiptService
   860	    from astrid.core.repositories.runs import RunRepository
   861	    from astrid.core.repositories.tasks import TaskRepository
   862	    from astrid.core.repositories.projects import ProjectRepository
   863	    from astrid.core.repositories.media import MediaRepository
   864	    from astrid.core.io.media_import import managed_media_path
   865	    from astrid.core.task_executor import CapabilityTaskHandler, ExecutionService
   866	    from astrid.core.kernel.read import schema_registry_context
   867	    from astrid.core.integrations.reigh.bridge_service import derive_database_path
   868	    if registry is None:
   869	        from astrid.core.schema_packs.standard import build_standard_registry
   870	
   871	        registry = build_standard_registry()
   872	    db_path = derive_database_path(projects_root)
   873	    db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   874	    writer = DatabaseWriter(db_path, registry)
   875	    try:
   876	        events = EventAppendService(registry)
   877	        receipts = ReceiptService()
   878	        runs = RunRepository(events=events, receipts=receipts)
   879	        tasks = TaskRepository(events=events, receipts=receipts)
   880	        projects = ProjectRepository(events=events, receipts=receipts)
   881	        media_repo = MediaRepository(events=events, receipts=receipts, projects_root=projects_root)
   882	        project_id = project if project else "default"
   883	        try:
   884	            UnitOfWork(writer).run(lambda u: projects.create(u, slug=project_id, name=project_id, settings={}, idempotency_key=f"proj:{project_id}", project_id=project_id))
   885	        except Exception:
   886	            pass
   887	        # Public SDK callers address projects by slug or id.  RunRepository
   888	        # stores the canonical project id, so resolve the reference after the
   889	        # idempotent create attempt rather than leaking a slug into runs.
   890	        project_id = projects.resolve(writer, project_id)
   891	        spec_payload = {"capability_id": capability.id, "inputs": dict(inputs or {}), "outputs": dict(outputs or {}), "project": project, "kind": str(kind), "extra_pack_roots": list(extra_pack_roots)}
   892	        idempotency_payload = dict(spec_payload)
   893	        if idempotency_context is not None:
   894	            idempotency_payload["authority_context"] = dict(idempotency_context)
   895	        idempotency_key = compute_spec_hash(idempotency_payload, [])
   896	        # Deterministic ids for idempotent replay: run_id derived from
   897	        # idempotency_key so identical retry returns same run_id via receipt
   898	        # (request_hash includes run_id). Child task_id also deterministic
   899	        # so request identity is stable; receipt replay returns same ids.
   900	        deterministic_run_id = hashlib.sha256(f"run:{idempotency_key}".encode()).hexdigest()[:26]
   901	        deterministic_task_id = hashlib.sha256(f"task:{idempotency_key}:0".encode()).hexdigest()[:26]
   902	        child_spec = {"capability_id": capability.id, "inputs": dict(inputs or {}), "outputs": dict(outputs or {}), "project": project, "kind": str(kind), "extra_pack_roots": list(extra_pack_roots)}
   903	        def _create(u):
   904	            return runs.create(
   905	                u,
   906	                project_id=project_id,
   907	                children=[{"capability": capability.id, "spec": child_spec, "input_manifest": [], "task_id": deterministic_task_id}],
   908	                idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
   909	                kind=capability.capability_type,
   910	                title=capability.id,
   911	                input=child_spec,
   912	                run_id=deterministic_run_id,
   913	            )
   914	        fanout = UnitOfWork(writer).run(_create)
   915	        run_id = fanout.run_id
   916	        task_id = fanout.task_ids[0] if fanout.task_ids else None
   917	        if task_id is None:
   918	            raise RuntimeError("kernel admission produced no task")
   919	        # If run already terminal (idempotent replay after success), skip re-drive.
   920	        # Query run status without receipt side-effects.

    32	def _read_registry(
    33	    registry: FrozenSchemaPackRegistry | None,
    34	) -> FrozenSchemaPackRegistry:
    35	    """Return the database composition used by this read.
    36	
    37	    Project databases are the standard Astrid composition, not core-only
    38	    stores: their migration ledger includes the in-tree timeline, shots, and
    39	    references packs.  Core-only readers therefore fail with
    40	    ``MigrationTooNewError`` as soon as one of those packs has been used.  A
    41	    caller handling an explicitly extended composition can still provide its
    42	    already-composed registry; the default only chooses the standard in-tree
    43	    composition and never weakens migration validation.
    44	    """
    45	
    46	    if registry is None:
    47	        registry = _ACTIVE_SCHEMA_REGISTRY.get()
    48	    if registry is not None:
    49	        return registry
    50	    from astrid.core.schema_packs.standard import build_standard_registry
    51	
    52	    return build_standard_registry()

    55	@contextmanager
    56	def schema_registry_context(
    57	    registry: FrozenSchemaPackRegistry,
    58	) -> Iterator[None]:
    59	    """Bind one composed registry to nested canonical kernel reads.
    60	
    61	    Capability execution can perform a read after the outer SDK has admitted
    62	    the task.  A context variable carries the client's exact composition into
    63	    those in-process reads without a process-global mutable registry or an
    64	    ambient auto-discovery of arbitrary schemas.
    65	    """
    66	
    67	    token = _ACTIVE_SCHEMA_REGISTRY.set(registry)
    68	    try:
    69	        yield
    70	    finally:
    71	        _ACTIVE_SCHEMA_REGISTRY.reset(token)

    74	def _resolve_project_id(conn: sqlite3.Connection, slug: str) -> str | None:
    75	    # Slug-first, then raw id fallback. Narrow to sqlite3.Error at caller.
    76	    row = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM projects WHERE slug = ?", (slug,)).fetchone()
    77	    if row is not None:
    78	        return str(row[0] if row[0] is not None else row["id"])
    79	    row2 = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM projects WHERE id = ?", (slug,)).fetchone()
    80	    if row2 is not None:
    81	        return str(row2[0] if row2[0] is not None else row2["id"])
    82	    return None

    85	def kernel_run_info(
    86	    slug: str,
    87	    run_id: str,
    88	    *,
    89	    projects_root: str | Path | None = None,
    90	    root: str | Path | None = None,
    91	    registry: FrozenSchemaPackRegistry | None = None,
    92	) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    93	    """Return kernel run info for one project/run, or None.
    94	
    95	    Resolves ``slug → project_id (ULID)`` correctly via the projects table
    96	    (no slug-as-id fallback leaking into ``runs.project_id``), then loads the
    97	    run row and first-child capability/spec. Uses :func:`open_database`
    98	    read-only; callers see ``sqlite3.Error`` only.
    99	    """
   100	    raw_root = projects_root if projects_root is not None else root
   101	    pr = resolve_projects_root(raw_root)
   102	    db_path = _db_path(pr)
   103	    if db_path is None or not db_path.is_file():
   104	        return None
   105	    try:
   106	        from astrid.core.store.database import open_database
   107	
   108	        conn = open_database(db_path, _read_registry(registry), read_only=True)
   109	    except (sqlite3.Error, FileNotFoundError, OSError):
   110	        return None

   121	def _owned_managed_locators(
   122	    requested: set[Path],
   123	    *,
   124	    projects_root: Path,
   125	    project_slug: str | None,
   126	) -> dict[Path, str]:
   127	    """Return exact managed locators owned by the active project.
   128	
   129	    A project render may consume Astrid's shared CAS media directory, but it
   130	    must not turn that directory into a general read root.  The registry's
   131	    exact absolute paths are intersected with the kernel's ``media`` ownership
   132	    rows for the active project.  The content hash is retained so the source
   133	    can be checked again immediately before staging.
   134	    """
   135	
   136	    if not requested or not project_slug:
   137	        return {}
   138	    database = _kernel_database_path(projects_root)
   139	    if database is None:
   140	        return {}
   141	    managed_root = (projects_root / ".astrid" / "media").resolve(strict=False)
   142	    try:
   143	        from astrid.core.schema_packs.standard import build_standard_registry
   144	        from astrid.core.store.database import open_database
   145	
   146	        connection = open_database(database, build_standard_registry(), read_only=True)
   147	    except (OSError, sqlite3.Error, ValueError):
   148	        return {}
   149	    try:
   150	        connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
   151	        project = connection.execute(
   152	            "SELECT id FROM projects WHERE slug = ? OR id = ? LIMIT 1",
   153	            (project_slug, project_slug),
   154	        ).fetchone()
   155	        if project is None:
   156	            return {}
   157	        rows = connection.execute(
   158	            "SELECT l.locator, m.content_hash "
   159	            "FROM media_locations AS l JOIN media AS m ON m.id = l.media_id "
   160	            "WHERE m.project_id = ? AND l.realm = 'managed_local'",
   161	            (str(project["id"]),),
   162	        ).fetchall()
   163	    except sqlite3.Error:
   164	        return {}
   165	    finally:
   166	        connection.close()
   167	
   168	    authorized: dict[Path, str] = {}
   169	    for row in rows:
   170	        try:
   171	            locator = Path(str(row["locator"])).expanduser().resolve(strict=False)
   172	            content_hash = str(row["content_hash"])
   173	        except (OSError, TypeError, ValueError):
   174	            continue
   175	        # The ownership row alone is not enough: only canonical files inside

   311	def _is_secret_name(name: str) -> bool:
   312	    """Return True when *name* is a ``.env`` or otherwise secret-bearing file."""
   313	    lowered = name.lower()
   314	    if lowered == ".env" or lowered.startswith(".env.") or lowered.endswith(".env"):
   315	        return True
   316	    if any(marker in lowered for marker in _SECRET_NAME_MARKERS):
   317	        return True
   318	    return lowered.endswith(_SECRET_FILE_SUFFIXES)

   340	def _online_backup(
   341	    db_path: Path, dest_db: Path
   342	) -> tuple[tuple[tuple[str, int, str, str], ...], int]:
   343	    """Take a consistent online snapshot of *db_path* into *dest_db*.
   344	
   345	    Uses ``sqlite3.Connection.backup`` (the online backup API), which reads a
   346	    transactionally consistent snapshot without blocking the source writer.
   347	    The snapshot is written to a sibling temp file and atomically moved into
   348	    place so an idempotent re-backup never observes a half-written file.
   349	    """
   350	    source = sqlite3.connect(read_only_uri(db_path), uri=True, isolation_level=None)
   351	    try:
   352	        packs = _read_migration_state(source)
   353	        sqlite_pages = int(source.execute("PRAGMA page_count").fetchone()[0])
   354	        dest_db.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   355	        fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
   356	            prefix=f".{BACKUP_DATABASE_NAME}.", suffix=".tmp", dir=dest_db.parent
   357	        )
   358	        os.close(fd)
   359	        tmp_path = Path(tmp_name)
   360	        try:
   361	            destination = sqlite3.connect(str(tmp_path))
   362	            try:
   363	                source.backup(destination)
   364	                # The backup API copies the source header verbatim, which
   365	                # carries journal_mode=WAL; a single-file WAL snapshot cannot
   366	                # be opened read-only (its -shm index is missing), so restore
   367	                # validation fails on it. Rewrite the header to DELETE mode so
   368	                # the snapshot is a portable, self-contained single file.
   369	                destination.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE")
   370	            finally:
   371	                destination.close()
   372	            os.replace(tmp_path, dest_db)
   373	        finally:
   374	            tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
   375	        return packs, sqlite_pages
   376	    finally:
   377	        source.close()
   378

  1253	def _validate_staged_database(staged_db: Path) -> None:
  1254	    """Validate a staged database read-only; raise on any corruption/incompat.
  1255	
  1256	    Checks, in order: ``PRAGMA quick_check`` (page-level integrity),
  1257	    ``PRAGMA foreign_key_check`` (referential integrity), and a schema-version
  1258	    probe against the current standard registry (too-new schema, name drift,
  1259	    checksum drift, or an unregistered pack). The staged file is opened
  1260	    ``mode=ro`` and never mutated.
  1261	    """
  1262	    try:
  1263	        conn = sqlite3.connect(
  1264	            f"file:{staged_db}?mode=ro", uri=True, isolation_level=None
  1265	        )
  1266	    except sqlite3.Error as exc:
  1267	        raise RestoreValidationError(
  1268	            f"cannot open staged database read-only: {exc}"
  1269	        ) from exc
  1270	    try:
  1271	        try:
  1272	            quick = conn.execute("PRAGMA quick_check").fetchone()[0]
  1273	        except sqlite3.Error as exc:
  1274	            raise RestoreValidationError(f"quick_check failed: {exc}") from exc
  1275	        if quick != "ok":
  1276	            raise RestoreValidationError(f"quick_check reported: {quick!r}")
  1277	        try:
  1278	            fk_rows = conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_key_check").fetchall()
  1279	        except sqlite3.Error as exc:
  1280	            raise RestoreValidationError(f"foreign_key_check failed: {exc}") from exc
  1281	        if fk_rows:
  1282	            raise RestoreValidationError(
  1283	                f"foreign_key_check found {len(fk_rows)} violation(s)"
  1284	            )
  1285	    finally:
  1286	        conn.close()
  1287	
  1288	    from astrid.core.schema_packs.standard import build_standard_registry
  1289	
  1290	    registry = build_standard_registry()
  1291	    try:
  1292	        probe_database(staged_db, registry)
  1293	    except MigrationError as exc:
  1294	        raise RestoreValidationError(
  1295	            f"schema-version incompatibility: {exc}"
  1296	        ) from exc
  1297	
  1298	
  1299	def _normalize_staged_database_journal(staged_db: Path) -> None:
  1300	    """Ensure a staged DB can be opened read-only without WAL sidecars."""
  1301	    try:
  1302	        conn = sqlite3.connect(str(staged_db), isolation_level=None)
  1303	    except sqlite3.Error as exc:
  1304	        raise RestoreValidationError(
  1305	            f"cannot normalize staged database journal mode: {exc}"
  1306	        ) from exc
  1307	    try:
  1308	        try:
  1309	            mode = conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE").fetchone()[0]
  1310	        except sqlite3.Error as exc:
  1311	            raise RestoreValidationError(
  1312	                f"cannot normalize staged database journal mode: {exc}"
  1313	            ) from exc
  1314	        if str(mode).lower() != "delete":
  1315	            raise RestoreValidationError(
  1316	                f"staged database retained unsupported journal mode: {mode!r}"
  1317	            )
  1318	    finally:
  1319	        conn.close()
  1320	    for suffix in _RESTORE_DATABASE_SIDECARS:
  1800	            _remove_restore_path(Path(f"{live_db}{suffix}"))
  1801	        os.replace(staged_db, live_db)
  1802	        state = _write_restore_journal(state, phase="database_published")
  1803	        _restore_boundary("database_published", journal=journal_path)
  1804	        _remove_restore_path(live_media)
  1805	        os.replace(staged_media, live_media)
  1806	        state = _write_restore_journal(state, phase="media_published")
  1807	        _restore_boundary("media_published", journal=journal_path)
  1808	    except BaseException:
  1809	        # A normal exception gets the same deterministic recovery as a fresh
  1810	        # process. Hard-death hooks use os._exit and never reach this block.
  1811	        try:
  1812	            _recover_restore_transaction(journal_path, expected_database=live_db)
  1813	        except BaseException:
  1814	            # Preserve the journal for the next standard composition if the
  1815	            # in-process rollback itself cannot complete.
  1816	            pass
  1817	        raise
  1818	    _finish_restore_transaction(state)
  1819	
  1820	
  1821	_LIVE_DATA_PROBE_TABLES = (
  1822	    "projects",
  1823	    "event_streams",
  1824	    "events",
  1825	    "media",
  1826	    "command_receipts",
  1827	)
  1828	"""Tables whose non-emptiness means the live database holds real content."""
  1829	
  1830	
  1831	def _live_database_holds_data(live_db: str | Path) -> bool:
  1832	    """Return True when an existing live database holds real content.
  1833	
  1834	    An absent database is empty by definition. A present database counts as
  1835	    holding data when any content table has rows — i.e. anything beyond a
  1836	    freshly initialized root, whose tables are all empty. A present database
  1837	    that cannot be probed read-only (corrupt bytes, foreign schema, missing
  1838	    migration rows, unreadable WAL) **also** counts as holding data:
  1839	    restore must never silently discard bytes it cannot inspect.
  1840	    """
  1841	    path = Path(live_db)
  1842	    if not _restore_is_file(path):
  1843	        return False
  1844	    try:
  1845	        conn = sqlite3.connect(read_only_uri(path), uri=True)
  1846	    except sqlite3.Error:
  1847	        return True
  1848	    try:
  1849	        try:
  1850	            if not read_schema_migrations(conn):
  1851	                return True
  1852	        except sqlite3.Error:
  1853	            return True
  1854	        for table in _LIVE_DATA_PROBE_TABLES:
  1855	            try:
  1856	                row = conn.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {table}").fetchone()
  1857	            except sqlite3.Error:
  1858	                return True
  1859	            if row is not None and int(row[0]) > 0:
  1860	                return True
  1861	        return False
  1862	    finally:
  1863	        conn.close()
  1864	
  1865	
  1866	def restore_backup(
  1867	    backup_path: str | Path,
  1868	    projects_root: str | Path | None = None,
  1869	    *,
  1870	    allow_overwrite: bool = False,
  1871	) -> RestoreResult:
  1872	    """Restore a backup into the managed database and media tree atomically.
  1873	
  1874	    Stages the backup under ``.astrid/.restore-staging/``, validates the staged
  1875	    database read-only (quick_check + foreign_key_check + schema-version), and
  1876	    only then swaps it into place. A corrupt or incompatible backup raises
  1877	    :class:`RestoreValidationError` and leaves live data untouched.
  1878	
  1879	    Safety default: when the target root already holds a live database with
  1880	    content, the restore refuses with :class:`RestoreValidationError` unless
     1	"""Read-only data diagnostics for Astrid (m6 v10 doctor rewrite).
     2	
     3	This module replaces the old environment checks (executor/orchestrator
     4	registries, element catalog, vibecomfy/remotion/runpod probing) with exactly
     5	six read-only v10 checks over the managed database and media tree:
     6	
     7	1. ``sqlite_quick_check`` — open the database ``mode=ro`` and run
     8	   ``PRAGMA quick_check`` (page-level integrity);
     9	2. ``fk_integrity`` — ``PRAGMA foreign_key_check`` (referential integrity);
    10	3. ``schema_versions`` — the ``schema_migrations`` rows (core + installed
    11	   pack versions) compared against the current standard registry;
    12	4. ``media_paths`` — the managed-media root and ``sha256/`` digest tree are
    13	   accessible, managed and external locators resolve to the recorded bytes,
    14	   and any orphaned ``.staging`` directories are reported;
    15	5. ``data_paths`` — the projects root and ``.astrid/`` are accessible;
    16	6. ``python_version`` — the Python 3.10+ floor.
    17	
    18	The doctor is **strictly read-only**: it never runs ``VACUUM``, ``REINDEX``,
    19	or any repair, and it never opens a writable connection. On a missing or
    20	corrupt database it fails closed — an existing managed root with a missing or
    21	corrupt database reports ``fail`` with a stable detail, the overall ``ok`` is
    22	``false``, and the process exits ``1``. A root with no ``.astrid`` store yet is
    23	reported as ``uninitialized`` (with ``ok: true`` and exit ``0``), so the
    24	first-run diagnostic distinguishes a setup state from an unhealthy store.
    25	
    26	The JSON surface is stable: ``{"ok": bool, "checks": [{"name", "status",
    27	"detail", "required"}, ...], "state": "uninitialized|ready|unhealthy",
    28	"next_action": string | null}``. A pristine root remains healthy
    29	(``ok: true``, exit ``0``) while exposing the one setup action needed next.
    30	"""

    37	import sys
    38	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass

    40

    42	from astrid.core.io.media_import import managed_media_path, sha256_file_bytes
    43	from astrid.core.kernel.database import resolve_kernel_database_authority
    44	from astrid.core.migrations.runner import MigrationError, probe_database

    46	Status = str
    47

    51	MEDIA_DIR_NAME = "media"
    52	SHA256_DIR_NAME = "sha256"
    53	STAGING_DIR_NAME = ".staging"

    57	    "expected on a brand-new projects root; run "
    58	    "`astrid projects create <slug> --name <Name>` to initialize it"
    59	)

    62	    "Initialize a project with `python3 -m astrid projects create "

    67	def _is_uninitialized_root(root: Path) -> bool:
    68	    """Return true only when no managed store has been started yet."""
    69	
    70	    authority = resolve_kernel_database_authority(root)
    71	    return not (root / MANAGED_DIR_NAME).exists() and not authority.exists

    74	def _uninitialized_check(name: str, detail: str) -> DoctorCheck:
    75	    return DoctorCheck(name=name, status="uninitialized", detail=detail, required=False)

    78	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    79	class DoctorCheck:
    80	    name: str
    81	    status: Status
    82	    detail: str
    83	    required: bool = True
    84	
    85	    def failed(self, *, strict_optional: bool = False) -> bool:
    86	        if self.status == "fail":
    87	            return True
    88	        return strict_optional and not self.required and self.status == "warn"

    91	def run_checks(
    92	    *, projects_root: str | Path | None = None
    93	) -> tuple[DoctorCheck, ...]:
    94	    """Run the six read-only v10 checks against the resolved projects root."""
    95	    root = resolve_projects_root(projects_root)
    96	    return (
    97	        _check_python_version(),
    98	        _check_data_paths(root),
    99	        _check_media_paths(root),
   100	        _check_sqlite_quick_check(root),
   101	        _check_fk_integrity(root),
   102	        _check_schema_versions(root),
   103	    )

   105	
   106	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
   107	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
   108	        prog="python3 -m astrid doctor",
   109	        description="Check the Astrid managed data environment (read-only).",
   110	    )
   111	    parser.add_argument(
   112	        "--json", action="store_true", help="Emit machine-readable diagnostics."
   113	    )
   114	    parser.add_argument(
   115	        "--strict-optional",
   116	        action="store_true",
   117	        help="Treat optional warnings as failures.",
   118	    )
   119	    parser.add_argument(
   120	        "--projects-root",
   121	        default=None,
   122	        help="Projects root (default: ASTRID_PROJECTS_ROOT or the default root).",
   123	    )
   124	    return parser
   125	
   126	
   127	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   128	    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
   129	    checks = run_checks(projects_root=args.projects_root)
   130	    failed = any(
   131	        check.failed(strict_optional=args.strict_optional) for check in checks
   132	    )
   133	    state = (
   134	        "unhealthy"
   135	        if failed
   136	        else "uninitialized"
   137	        if any(check.status == "uninitialized" for check in checks)
   138	        else "ready"
   139	    )
   140	    next_action = NEW_ROOT_NEXT_ACTION if state == "uninitialized" else None
   141	    if args.json:
   142	        payload = {
   143	            "ok": not failed,
   144	            "checks": [asdict(check) for check in checks],
   145	            "state": state,
   146	            "next_action": next_action,
   147	        }
   148	        print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
   149	    else:
   150	        print("Astrid doctor")
   151	        print(f"state: {state}")
   152	        if next_action is not None:
   153	            print(f"next action: {next_action}")
   154	        for check in checks:
   155	            print(f"[{check.status}] {check.name}: {check.detail}")
   156	    return 1 if failed else 0

   164	def _check_python_version() -> DoctorCheck:
   165	    version = sys.version_info
   166	    if version < MIN_PYTHON:
   167	        return DoctorCheck(
   168	            name="python_version",
   169	            status="fail",
   170	            detail=(
   171	                f"Python {MIN_PYTHON[0]}.{MIN_PYTHON[1]}+ required; "
   172	                f"found {version.major}.{version.minor}.{version.micro}"
   173	            ),
   174	        )
   175	    return DoctorCheck(
   176	        name="python_version",
   177	        status="ok",
   178	        detail=f"{version.major}.{version.minor}.{version.micro}",
   179	    )
   180	
   620	    if rows:
   621	        return DoctorCheck(
   622	            name="fk_integrity",
   623	            status="fail",
   624	            detail=f"{len(rows)} foreign key violation(s)",
   625	        )
   626	    return DoctorCheck(
   627	        name="fk_integrity", status="ok", detail="no foreign key violations"
   628	    )

   631	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   632	# schema_versions
   633	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   635	
   636	def _check_schema_versions(root: Path) -> DoctorCheck:
   637	    from astrid.core.schema_packs.standard import build_standard_registry
   638	
   639	    db_path = _database_path(root)
   640	    registry = build_standard_registry()
   641	    try:
   642	        probe = probe_database(db_path, registry)
   643	    except MigrationError as exc:
   644	        return DoctorCheck(
   645	            name="schema_versions",
   646	            status="fail",
   647	            detail=str(exc),
   648	        )
   649	    except sqlite3.Error as exc:
   650	        # Fail closed on a corrupt/unreadable database file: a doctor that
   651	        # raises out of `run_checks` would crash the CLI instead of returning
   652	        # the stable `{"ok": false}` envelope, so surface the read failure as
   653	        # a failed check (matching sqlite_quick_check / fk_integrity).
   654	        return DoctorCheck(
   655	            name="schema_versions",
   656	            status="fail",
   657	            detail=f"cannot read database schema: {exc}",
   658	        )
   659	    if not probe.exists:
   660	        if _is_uninitialized_root(root):
   661	            return _uninitialized_check(
   662	                "schema_versions",
   663	                f"database not initialized: {db_path} ({NEW_ROOT_GUIDANCE})",
   664	            )
   665	        return DoctorCheck(
   666	            name="schema_versions",
   667	            status="fail",
   668	            detail=f"database missing: {db_path} ({NEW_ROOT_GUIDANCE})",
   669	        )
   670	    by_pack: dict[str, int] = {}
   671	    for applied in probe.applied:
   672	        by_pack[applied.pack] = applied.version
   673	    detail = ", ".join(
   674	        f"{pack}={version}" for pack, version in sorted(by_pack.items())
   675	    )
   676	    return DoctorCheck(
   677	        name="schema_versions",
   678	        status="ok",
   679	        detail=detail or "no applied migrations",
   680	    )
   681

   684	    raise SystemExit(main())
     1	"""SQLite database opening: read-only probe, writable PRAGMAs, migrations.
     2	
     3	(m1 plan step 5.) :func:`open_database` is the only supported way to open an
     4	Astrid database:
     5	
     6	1. It probes the database **read-only** through the migration runner
     7	   (:func:`astrid.core.migrations.runner.probe_database`), rejecting too-new
     8	   schemas, name drift, and exact-byte checksum drift before any mutation is
     9	   possible.
    10	2. For a writable open it applies the declared connection-level PRAGMAs
    11	   (:data:`astrid.core.migrations.catalog.CONNECTION_PRAGMAS`) and then
    12	   applies pending migrations dependency-ordered and transactionally.
    13	
    14	The writable PRAGMAs are inspectable afterwards through
    15	:func:`inspect_connection_pragmas`, so tests and operators can prove
    16	``foreign_keys``, ``journal_mode``, ``synchronous``, and ``busy_timeout``
    17	settings on a live connection.
    18	
    19	This module never imports the capability-pack loader or discovery machinery,
    20	and a read-only open never mutates the database file.
    21	"""
    22	
    23	from __future__ import annotations
    24	
    25	import sqlite3
    26	from pathlib import Path
    27	from typing import Any
    28	
    29	from astrid.core.migrations.catalog import CONNECTION_PRAGMAS
    30	from astrid.core.migrations.runner import (
    31	    apply_pending_migrations,
    32	    probe_database,
    33	    read_only_uri,
    34	)
    35	from astrid.core.schema_packs.registry import FrozenSchemaPackRegistry
    36	
    37	PRAGMA_QUERIES: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (
    38	    ("foreign_keys", "PRAGMA foreign_keys"),
    39	    ("journal_mode", "PRAGMA journal_mode"),
    40	    ("synchronous", "PRAGMA synchronous"),
    41	    ("busy_timeout", "PRAGMA busy_timeout"),
    42	)
    43	"""Inspectable writable PRAGMA surface (``name -> query``)."""
    44	
    45	
    46	def apply_connection_pragmas(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    47	    """Apply the declared writable connection-level PRAGMAs.
    48	
    49	    Each entry of :data:`CONNECTION_PRAGMAS` is a ``key = value`` fragment;
    50	    this runs them exactly as cataloged on a writable connection.
    51	    """
    52	    for pragma in CONNECTION_PRAGMAS:
    53	        conn.execute(f"PRAGMA {pragma}")
    54	
    55	
    56	def inspect_connection_pragmas(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> dict[str, Any]:
    57	    """Return the live values of the inspectable writable PRAGMAs.
    58	
    59	    Example: ``{'foreign_keys': 1, 'journal_mode': 'wal', 'synchronous': 1,
    60	    'busy_timeout': 5000}``.
    61	    """
    62	    return {
    63	        name: conn.execute(query).fetchone()[0] for name, query in PRAGMA_QUERIES
    64	    }
    65	
    66	
    67	def open_database(
    68	    path: str | Path,
    69	    registry: FrozenSchemaPackRegistry,
    70	    *,
    71	    read_only: bool = False,
    72	) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    73	    """Open (and, for writable opens, migrate) an Astrid database.
    74	
    75	    Read-only opens perform the same nonmutating incompatibility probe and
    76	    then open with ``mode=ro``; they never apply PRAGMAs or migrations.
    77	    Writable opens probe, apply the declared PRAGMAs, apply pending
    78	    migrations forward-only and exactly once, and return the configured
    79	    connection.
    80	    """
    81	    db_path = Path(path)
    82	    probe = probe_database(db_path, registry)
    83	    if read_only:
    84	        if not probe.exists:
    85	            raise FileNotFoundError(
    86	                f"cannot open database read-only: {db_path} does not exist"
    87	            )
    88	        return sqlite3.connect(
    89	            read_only_uri(db_path), uri=True, isolation_level=None
    90	        )
    91	    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(db_path), isolation_level=None)
    92	    try:
    93	        apply_connection_pragmas(conn)
    94	        apply_pending_migrations(conn, registry, probe)
    95	    except Exception:
    96	        conn.close()
    97	        raise
    98	    return conn
    99

   102	    "PRAGMA_QUERIES",
   103	    "apply_connection_pragmas",
   104	    "inspect_connection_pragmas",
   105	    "open_database",
   106	]
     1	"""Dedicated single-writer SQLite service with FIFO submission.
     2	
     3	(m1 plan step 6.) One writer thread owns exactly one writable ``sqlite3``
     4	connection opened through :func:`astrid.core.store.database.open_database`.
     5	Repository callers submit short synchronous command callbacks via
     6	:meth:`DatabaseWriter.submit`; the writer thread executes them in FIFO order
     7	and returns the result (or re-raises the callback's exception) to the
     8	submitting caller. The owned connection never escapes the writer thread:
     9	callbacks receive only a :class:`WriterSession` facade with typed query and
    10	execute operations and no path back to the connection object.
    11	
    12	Design rules kept here:
    13	
    14	- One writer thread, one owned connection, one FIFO queue
    15	  (``queue.Queue``, so submission order is execution order).
    16	- ``submit()`` is synchronous: it blocks until the callback completes and
    17	  surfaces the callback's exception unchanged, except that SQLite busy
    18	  errors (``database is locked`` / ``database table is locked``) are
    19	  translated to the typed :class:`WriterBusyError` so callers never depend
    20	  on driver-specific messages.
    21	- Submissions after :meth:`DatabaseWriter.close` raise the typed
    22	  :class:`WriterShutdownError`.
    23	- :meth:`DatabaseWriter.close` deterministically drains the queue, stops
    24	  the writer thread, and closes the owned connection; the connection is
    25	  touched only by the writer thread, including its final close.
    26	- Read traffic never shares the write connection:
    27	  :meth:`DatabaseWriter.read_only_connection` yields a separate read-only
    28	  connection opened through the nonmutating read-only open path.
    29	
    30	This module never imports the capability-pack loader or discovery
    31	machinery and never hands the write connection (or any ``sqlite3``
    32	connection) to callers. Transaction control (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK) is
    33	owned by the kernel unit of work (plan step 7), never by writer callers:
    34	the session rejects transaction-control statements with the typed
    35	:class:`TransactionControlError`, and callbacks that submit work from the
    36	writer thread are rejected up front (they would deadlock the FIFO queue).
    37	When a unit of work is active, an opt-in statement observer
    38	(``on_statement`` on the unit of work) is notified after every SQL
    39	statement boundary, including BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, so tests
    40	can observe the exact transaction shape without any environment switch.
    41	
    42	Rows returned by the session are ``sqlite3.Row`` objects (the writer
    43	connection uses ``row_factory = sqlite3.Row``), so callers may address
    44	columns by name or position.
    45	"""
    46	
    47	from __future__ import annotations
    48	
    49	import queue
    50	import sqlite3
    51	import threading
    52	from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator, Sequence
    53	from contextlib import contextmanager
    54	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    55	from pathlib import Path
    56	from typing import Any
    57	
    58	from astrid.core.schema_packs.registry import FrozenSchemaPackRegistry
    59	from astrid.core.store.database import open_database
    60	
    61	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    62	# Errors
    63	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    64	
    65	
    66	class WriterError(RuntimeError):
    67	    """Base error for the dedicated single-writer service."""
    68	
    69	
    70	class WriterBusyError(WriterError):
    71	    """Raised when a write callback hit the SQLite busy timeout.
    72	
    73	    The configured ``busy_timeout`` bounds lock contention; when SQLite
    74	    still reports a locked database after that bound, this typed error is
    75	    raised to the submitting caller.
    76	    """
    77	
    78	
    79	class WriterShutdownError(WriterError):
    80	    """Raised when work is submitted after the writer has been closed."""
    81	
    82	
    83	class TransactionControlError(WriterError):
    84	    """Raised when a caller attempts to control transactions directly.
    85	
    86	    Transaction control (BEGIN IMMEDIATE / COMMIT / ROLLBACK / SAVEPOINT /
    87	    RELEASE) is owned by the kernel unit of work. The writer session
    88	    rejects such statements, and its private transaction methods raise
    89	    this error on invalid transitions (begin-within-transaction, or
    90	    commit/rollback with no active transaction).
    91	    """
    92	
    93	
    94	# Statements that would seize or release transaction control. Any SQL
    95	# whose first keyword is one of these is rejected on the writer session.
    96	_TRANSACTION_CONTROL_KEYWORDS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    97	    {"begin", "commit", "end", "rollback", "savepoint", "release"}
    98	)
    99	
   100	
   101	def _first_statement_keyword(sql: str) -> str | None:
   102	    """Return the lowercased first keyword of ``sql``, skipping comments."""
   103	    text = sql
   104	    while True:
   105	        text = text.lstrip()
   106	        if text.startswith("--"):
   107	            newline = text.find("\n")
   108	            if newline == -1:
   109	                return None
   110	            text = text[newline + 1 :]
   111	            continue
   112	        if text.startswith("/*"):
   113	            close = text.find("*/")
   114	            if close == -1:
   115	                return None
   116	            text = text[close + 2 :]
   117	            continue
   118	        break
   119	    if not text:
   120	        return None
   121	    return text.split(None, 1)[0].lower()
   122	
   123	
   124	class _Sentinel:
   125	    """Unique marker used to stop the writer thread (never a work item)."""
   126	
   127	
   128	_SENTINEL = _Sentinel()
   129	
   130	
   131	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   132	# Non-escaping session facade
   133	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   134	
   135	
   136	class WriterSession:
   137	    """Typed, non-escaping facade over the writer's owned connection.
   138	
   139	    Exposes exactly the query/execute operations callbacks need. There is
   140	    deliberately no public attribute that yields the underlying
   141	    ``sqlite3.Connection``: the connection is owned by the writer thread and
   142	    transaction control is owned by the kernel unit of work (plan step 7).
   143	    Transaction-control statements (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/SAVEPOINT/
   144	    RELEASE) are rejected with :class:`TransactionControlError`.
   145	
   146	    Rows are ``sqlite3.Row`` objects (the writer connection uses
   147	    ``row_factory = sqlite3.Row``).
   148	    """
   149	
   150	    __slots__ = (
   151	        "_connection",
   152	        "_in_transaction",
   153	        "_statement_observer",
   154	    )
   155	
   156	    def __init__(self, connection: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
   157	        self._connection = connection
   158	        self._in_transaction = False
   159	        self._statement_observer: Callable[[str, str, tuple[Any, ...]], None] | None = None
   160	
   161	    # -- public typed operations ----------------------------------------
   162	
   163	    def execute(
   164	        self, sql: str, parameters: Sequence[Any] = ()
   165	    ) -> sqlite3.Cursor:
   166	        """Execute one statement on the writer's connection.
   167	
   168	        The connection runs in autocommit (``isolation_level=None``); the
   169	        unit of work owns explicit transaction boundaries. Returns the
   170	        cursor so callers can read ``lastrowid``/``rowcount``.
   171	        """
   172	        self._check_transaction_control(sql)
   173	        cursor = self._connection.execute(sql, parameters)
   174	        self._notify("statement", sql, parameters)
   175	        return cursor
   176	
   177	    def query(
   178	        self, sql: str, parameters: Sequence[Any] = ()
   179	    ) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
   180	        """Execute one read statement and return every row."""

   306	def _load_pack_executors_from_packs(
   307	    packs: Iterable[Any],
   308	) -> tuple[ExecutorDefinition, ...]:
   309	    executors: list[ExecutorDefinition] = []
   310	    for pack in packs:
   311	        # Per-pack fault tolerance: one broken content manifest (e.g. an
   312	        # installed external pack whose executor.yaml fails schema
   313	        # validation) must not abort the whole discovery/invoke. The pack is
   314	        # skipped with a warning; pack-alignment failures
   315	        # (``PackValidationError`` from ``validate_content_id_in_pack``)
   316	        # still propagate — a misplaced id is a packaging contract breach,
   317	        # not a bad manifest.
   318	        try:
   319	            for root in iter_executor_roots(pack):
   320	                for executor in load_folder_executors(root):
   321	                    validate_content_id_in_pack(executor.id, pack, content_type="executor")
   322	                    executors.append(_attach_pack_metadata(executor, pack.id, pack_root=pack.root, content_root=root))
   323	        except (ExecutorValidationError, ManifestParseError) as exc:
   324	            _LOGGER.warning(
   325	                "skipping pack %r: executor manifests failed validation: %s",
   326	                getattr(pack, "id", pack),
   327	                exc,
   328	            )
   329	            continue
   330	    return tuple(executors)

   186	@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
   187	def _load_default_registry_data(
   188	    active_theme_key: str | None,
   189	    project_root_key: str,
   190	    include_missing_roots: bool,
   191	    extra_pack_roots_key: tuple[str, ...],
   192	    include_installed: bool,
   193	) -> tuple[tuple[ElementDefinition, ...], ElementKindRegistry]:
   194	    """Parse the static element corpus once; return raw definitions.
   195	
   196	    The corpus (packs + default element sources) is static repo content.  A
   197	    fresh parse costs seconds of YAML work per call (measured: ~2s per load,
   198	    ~189 ``yaml.safe_load`` calls — a 93-event timeline replay that validates
   199	    four config events spends ~6s total).  Callers rebuild a fresh
   200	    :class:`ElementRegistry` from the cached raw definitions, so per-call
   201	    registry mutation (e.g. the element catalog's legacy-source registration)
   202	    never leaks into the shared cache.
   203	    """
   204	    project_root = Path(project_root_key)
   205	    pack_defs = tuple(
   206	        discovered.pack
   207	        for discovered in discover_pack_metadata(
   208	            project_root=project_root,
   209	            extra_pack_roots=tuple(Path(key) for key in extra_pack_roots_key),
   210	            include_installed=include_installed,
   211	            discover_packs_fn=discover_packs,
   212	        )
   213	    )
   214	    element_kind_registry = _element_kind_registry_for_packs(pack_defs)
   215	    elements: list[ElementDefinition] = list(
   216	        _load_pack_elements_from_packs(
   217	            pack_defs,
   218	            element_kind_registry=element_kind_registry,
   219	        )
   220	    )
   221	    for source in default_sources(
   222	        active_theme=Path(active_theme_key) if active_theme_key is not None else None,
   223	        project_root=project_root,
   224	    ):
   225	        if not source.root.exists():
   226	            if include_missing_roots:
   227	                source.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   228	            else:
   229	                continue
   230	        elements.extend(
   231	            load_source_elements(
   232	                source,
   233	                element_kind_registry=element_kind_registry,
   234	            )
   235	        )
   236	    return (tuple(elements), element_kind_registry)
   237	
   238	
   239	def clear_default_registry_cache() -> None:
   240	    """Drop the cached element corpus.
   241	
   242	    Test seam / hot-reload hook: tests that patch pack discovery must clear
   243	    this cache (the catalog's ``_clear_registry_cache`` does) so a re-discovered
   244	    corpus (e.g. a temp pack declaring a custom element kind) is re-parsed.
   245	    """
   246	    _load_default_registry_data.cache_clear()
   247	
   248	
   249	def load_default_registry(
   250	    *,
   251	    active_theme: str | Path | None = None,
   252	    project_root: str | Path = REPO_ROOT,
   253	    include_missing_roots: bool = False,
   254	    extra_pack_roots: tuple[str, ...] = (),
   255	    include_installed: bool = True,
   256	) -> ElementRegistry:
   257	    """Load the default element registry (corpus parse is cached).
   258	
   259	    Registry assembly stays per-call so callers may register additional
   260	    elements (e.g. the legacy-workspace source in the element catalog)
   261	    without polluting the shared corpus cache.
   262	    """
   263	    elements, element_kind_registry = _load_default_registry_data(
   264	        str(Path(active_theme).resolve()) if active_theme is not None else None,
   265	        str(Path(project_root).resolve()),
   266	        include_missing_roots,
   267	        tuple(str(Path(root).resolve()) for root in extra_pack_roots),
   268	        include_installed,
   269	    )
   270	    resolver = create_shared_alias_resolver()
   271	    _register_pack_aliases(resolver, {})  # M1: no aliases yet
   272	    registry = ElementRegistry(
   273	        alias_resolver=resolver,
   274	        element_kind_registry=element_kind_registry,
   275	    )
   276	    for element in elements:
   277	        registry.register(element)
   278	    return registry

   281	def default_sources(*, active_theme: str | Path | None = None, project_root: str | Path = REPO_ROOT) -> tuple[ElementSource, ...]:
   282	    theme_dir = _resolve_theme_dir(active_theme)
   283	    sources: list[ElementSource] = []
   284	    if theme_dir is not None:
   285	        sources.extend(
   286	            [
   287	                ElementSource("active_theme", theme_dir / "elements", 0, True),
   288	                ElementSource("active_theme", theme_dir, 0, True),
   289	            ]
   290	        )
   291	    return tuple(sources)

   293	
   294	def load_pack_elements(
   295	    *,
   296	    project_root: str | Path = REPO_ROOT,
   297	    extra_pack_roots: tuple[str, ...] = (),
   298	    include_installed: bool = True,
   299	    element_kind_registry: ElementKindRegistry | None = None,
   300	) -> tuple[ElementDefinition, ...]:
   301	    packs = tuple(
   302	        discovered.pack
   303	        for discovered in discover_pack_metadata(
   304	            project_root=project_root,
   305	            extra_pack_roots=extra_pack_roots,
   306	            include_installed=include_installed,
   307	            discover_packs_fn=discover_packs,
   308	        )
   309	    )
   310	    registry = element_kind_registry or _element_kind_registry_for_packs(packs)
   311	    return _load_pack_elements_from_packs(
   312	        packs,
   313	        element_kind_registry=registry,
   314	    )
   315	
   316	
   317	def load_source_elements(
   318	    source: ElementSource,
   319	    *,
   320	    element_kind_registry: ElementKindRegistry | None = None,
   321	) -> tuple[ElementDefinition, ...]:
   322	    from .schema import ELEMENT_MANIFEST_NAMES
   323	
   324	    elements: list[ElementDefinition] = []
   325	    registry = element_kind_registry or ELEMENT_KIND_REGISTRY
   326	    for kind in registry.canonical_kinds():
   327	        kind_root = source.root / kind
   328	        if not kind_root.is_dir():
   329	            continue
   330	        for child in sorted(kind_root.iterdir(), key=lambda path: path.name):
   331	            if not child.is_dir():
   332	                continue
   333	            if not any((child / name).is_file() for name in ELEMENT_MANIFEST_NAMES):
   334	                continue
   335	            try:
   336	                elements.append(
   337	                    load_element_definition(
   338	                        child,
   339	                        kind=kind,
   340	                        source=source.name,
   341	                        editable=source.editable,
   342	                        priority=source.priority,
   343	                        element_kind_registry=registry,
   344	                    )
   345	                )
   346	            except ElementValidationError as exc:
   347	                print(f"WARN skipping {child}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
   348	    return tuple(elements)
   349	
   350	
   351	def _element_kind_registry_for_packs(
   352	    packs: Iterable[PackDefinition],
   353	) -> ElementKindRegistry:
   354	    descriptors = []
   355	    for pack in packs:
   356	        descriptors.extend(pack_element_kind_descriptors(pack))
   357	    if not descriptors:
   358	        return ELEMENT_KIND_REGISTRY
   359	    try:
   360	        return ElementKindRegistry(descriptors=descriptors)
   361	    except ValueError as exc:
   362	        raise PackValidationError(f"pack.extensions.elements.kinds is invalid: {exc}") from exc
   363	
   364	
   365	def _load_pack_elements_from_packs(
   366	    packs: Iterable[PackDefinition],
   367	    *,
   368	    element_kind_registry: ElementKindRegistry,
   369	) -> tuple[ElementDefinition, ...]:
   370	    from .schema import ELEMENT_MANIFEST_NAMES
   371	
   372	    elements: list[ElementDefinition] = []
   373	    for pack in packs:
   374	        priority = 10 if pack.id == "local" else 30
   375	        # Per-pack fault tolerance: one broken element manifest (e.g. from an
   376	        # installed external pack) must not abort the whole discovery/invoke.
   377	        # The pack is skipped with a warning; pack-alignment failures
   378	        # (``PackValidationError`` from ``validate_element_pack_id``) still
   379	        # propagate — a misplaced pack_id is a packaging contract breach.
   380	        try:
   381	            for kind, root in iter_element_roots(
   382	                pack,
   383	                element_kind_registry=element_kind_registry,
   384	            ):
   385	                if not any((root / name).is_file() for name in ELEMENT_MANIFEST_NAMES):
   386	                    continue
   387	                element = load_element_definition(
   388	                    root,
   389	                    kind=kind,
   390	                    source=f"pack:{pack.id}",
   470	                str(exc),
   471	                code="alias_cycle",
   472	                requested_id=requested_id,
   473	                details={"alias_chain": chain},
   474	            ) from exc
   475	        return current, tuple(chain)

   497	def load_default_registries(
   498	    project_root: str | Path | None = None,
   499	    *,
   500	    extra_pack_roots: tuple[str, ...] = (),
   501	    include_installed: bool = True,
   502	) -> tuple[RendererRegistry, PlannerRegistry, FinalizerRegistry]:
   503	    """Discover static rendering manifests and build the three registries."""
   504	
   505	    root = REPO_ROOT if project_root is None else Path(project_root).resolve()
   506	    discovered = discover_pack_metadata(
   507	        project_root=root,
   508	        extra_pack_roots=extra_pack_roots,
   509	        include_installed=include_installed,
   510	        discover_packs_fn=discover_packs,
   511	    )
   512	    pack_trust = {
   513	        item.priority_index: _derive_pack_trust(item)
   514	        for item in discovered
   515	    }
   516	    override_store = OverrideStore(root)
   517	
   518	    renderers = RendererRegistry(
   519	        override_store=override_store,
   520	    )
   521	    planners = PlannerRegistry(
   522	        override_store=override_store,
   523	    )
   524	    finalizers = FinalizerRegistry(
   525	        override_store=override_store,
   526	    )
   527	
   528	    for item in discovered:
   529	        renderer_paths, planner_paths, finalizer_paths = pack_rendering_manifest_paths(
   530	            item.pack
   531	        )
   532	        _load_candidates(
   533	            renderers,
   534	            item,
   535	            renderer_paths,
   536	            RendererManifest,
   537	            pack_trust[item.priority_index],
   538	        )
   539	        _load_candidates(
   540	            planners,
   541	            item,
   542	            planner_paths,
   543	            PlannerManifest,
   544	            pack_trust[item.priority_index],
   545	        )
   546	        _load_candidates(
   547	            finalizers,
   548	            item,
   549	            finalizer_paths,
   550	            FinalizerManifest,
   551	            pack_trust[item.priority_index],
   552	        )
   553	
   554	    renderer_resolver, renderer_inspection_resolver = _build_alias_resolvers(
   555	        discovered,
   556	        kind="renderer",
   557	        pack_trust=pack_trust,
   558	        registry=renderers,
   559	        programmatic_aliases=_PROGRAMMATIC_RENDERER_ALIASES,
   560	        error_type=RendererRegistryError,
   561	    )
   562	    planner_resolver, planner_inspection_resolver = _build_alias_resolvers(
   563	        discovered,
   564	        kind="planner",
   565	        pack_trust=pack_trust,
   566	        registry=planners,
   567	        error_type=PlannerRegistryError,
   568	    )
   569	    finalizer_resolver, finalizer_inspection_resolver = _build_alias_resolvers(
   570	        discovered,
   115	        self,
   116	        backend_id: str,
   117	        *,
   118	        env_file: Path | None = None,
   119	        init_overrides: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
   120	    ) -> BackendAdapter:
   121	        return self.get_descriptor(backend_id).create(
   122	            env_file=env_file,
   123	            init_overrides=init_overrides,
   124	        )
   125

   127	def descriptors_from_pack(pack: PackDefinition) -> tuple[GenerationBackendDescriptor, ...]:
   128	    """Return inert backend descriptors declared by one pack manifest."""
   129	    generation = pack.extensions.get("generation")
   130	    if not isinstance(generation, dict):
   131	        return ()
   132	    backends = generation.get("backends")
   133	    if not isinstance(backends, list):
   134	        return ()
   135	
   136	    descriptors: list[GenerationBackendDescriptor] = []
   137	    for raw_backend in backends:
   138	        if not isinstance(raw_backend, dict):
   139	            continue
   140	        descriptors.append(
   141	            GenerationBackendDescriptor(
   142	                backend_id=str(raw_backend["id"]),
   143	                module=str(raw_backend["module"]),
   144	                class_name=str(raw_backend["class"]),
   145	                label=str(raw_backend.get("label", "")),
   146	                init_kwargs=dict(raw_backend.get("init_kwargs", {})),
   147	            )
   148	        )
   149	    return tuple(descriptors)
   150	
   151	
   152	def discover_generation_backend_descriptors(
   153	    *,
   154	    project_root: str | Path = REPO_ROOT,
   155	    extra_pack_roots: tuple[str, ...] = (),
   156	    include_installed: bool = True,
   157	) -> tuple[GenerationBackendDescriptor, ...]:
   158	    """Return pack-declared backend descriptors from discovered manifests."""
   159	    descriptors: list[GenerationBackendDescriptor] = []
   160	    for discovered_pack in discover_pack_metadata(
   161	        project_root=project_root,
   162	        extra_pack_roots=extra_pack_roots,
   163	        include_installed=include_installed,
   164	        discover_packs_fn=discover_packs,
   165	    ):
   166	        descriptors.extend(descriptors_from_pack(discovered_pack.pack))
   167	    return tuple(descriptors)

   130	def _scan_discovered_packs(descriptors: list[SkillDescriptor]) -> None:
   131	    """Append skills from installed and extra-root packs via shared metadata.
   132	
   133	    The source-tree walk above already covers source packs (including
   134	    manifest-less ones such as ``_core`` that pack discovery does not
   135	    enumerate), so this layer only adds the ``extra`` and ``installed``
   136	    source kinds. It reuses :func:`discover_pack_metadata` so skills track the
   137	    same roots and priority ordering as the executor/orchestrator/element
   138	    registries. Source packs win on id collision (they were appended first).
   139	    """
   140	    from astrid.core.pack.discovery import discover_pack_metadata
   141	
   142	    seen_ids = {descriptor.pack_id for descriptor in descriptors}
   143	    for discovered in discover_pack_metadata(include_installed=True):
   144	        if discovered.source_kind not in ("extra", "installed"):
   145	            continue
   146	        pack = discovered.pack
   147	        if pack.status == "deprecated" or pack.visibility == "hidden":
   148	            continue
   149	        pack_skill = discovered.pack_dir / "skill" / "SKILL.md"
   150	        if pack.id not in seen_ids and _try_add_skill(descriptors, pack_skill, pack.id):
   151	            seen_ids.add(pack.id)
   152	        for content_dir in (*discovered.executor_roots(), *discovered.orchestrator_roots()):
   153	            qualified_id = f"{pack.id}.{content_dir.name}"
   154	            nested_skill = content_dir / "skill" / "SKILL.md"
   155	            if qualified_id not in seen_ids and _try_add_skill(
   156	                descriptors, nested_skill, qualified_id
   157	            ):
   158	                seen_ids.add(qualified_id)
   159

   161	def list_skills(packs_dir: Path | None = None) -> list[SkillDescriptor]:
   162	    base = packs_dir or PACKS_DIR
   163	    descriptors: list[SkillDescriptor] = []
   164	    if not base.exists():
   165	        return descriptors
   166	    for pack_dir in sorted(base.iterdir()):
   167	        if not pack_dir.is_dir():
   168	            continue
   169	
   170	        manifest_path = pack_manifest_path(pack_dir)
   171	        pack = None
   172	        if manifest_path is not None:
   173	            try:
   174	                pack = load_pack_manifest(manifest_path)
   175	            except Exception:
   176	                pack = None
   177	        if pack is not None and (pack.status == "deprecated" or pack.visibility == "hidden"):
   178	            continue

     4	manifest mounts. It declares **exactly** the five product families —

     6	``timelines`` — and attaches the two manifest-declared nested mounts
     7	(``shots`` beneath ``timelines`` and ``references`` beneath ``media``)
     8	from the explicit in-tree schema-pack manifests (``cli_mounts``).
     9	
    10	Rules enforced before any dispatch (sense check SC25):
    11	
    12	- **Missing mounts** — a required manifest declaration (timelines, shots,
    13	  references) that the shipped manifests do not declare is rejected.
    14	- **Duplicate mounts** — two declarations for the same family or the same
    15	  mount path are rejected.
    16	- **Unexpected mounts** — a manifest declaring a family outside the frozen
    17	  declarations, or a declared family at a different path, is rejected.

    20	  there is no discovery, no scanning, and no injection point, so a mount
    21	  from any other source is impossible by construction.
    22	
    23	The product census also excludes the operational commands (``serve``,
    24	``doctor``, ``backup``): they are never part of the five-family product

   108	class ProductRegistryError(ValueError):
   109	    """Raised when the product mount registry is invalid.
   110	
   111	    Covers missing, duplicate, unexpected, and dynamically sourced mounts:
   112	    the registry fails closed before any dispatch can occur.

   116	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
   117	class ProductMount:
   118	    """One validated product mount declaration.
   119	
   120	    ``mount_path`` is the CLI path segments: ``("projects",)`` for a core
   121	    family, ``("timelines", "shots")`` for the nested shots family.
   122	    ``declared_by`` is ``"core"`` for the four kernel families and
   123	    ``"manifest:<pack-id>"`` for manifest-owned mounts (timelines, shots,
   124	    references).
   125	    """
   126	
   127	    family: str
   128	    mount_path: tuple[str, ...]
   129	    declared_by: str
   130	
   131	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
   132	        if not isinstance(self.family, str) or not self.family:
   133	            raise ProductRegistryError("family must be a non-empty string")
   134	        if not isinstance(self.mount_path, tuple) or not self.mount_path:
   135	            raise ProductRegistryError(
   136	                f"mount path for {self.family!r} must be non-empty"
   137	            )
   138	
   139	    @property
   140	    def mount_token(self) -> str:
   141	        """The space-joined CLI mount token (e.g. ``timelines shots``)."""
   142	        return " ".join(self.mount_path)
   143

   154	def read_manifest_cli_mounts() -> tuple[ManifestMount, ...]:
   155	    """Read ``cli_mounts`` from the three fixed in-tree pack manifests.
   156	
   157	    Only ``astrid/packs/{timeline,shots,references}/schema-pack.yaml`` is
   158	    consulted — the same explicit paths :func:`register_standard_schema_packs`
   159	    uses. There is no scanning, no loader, and no injection point: mounts
   160	    sourced anywhere else are impossible by construction (reject dynamic
   161	    mounts).
   162	    """
   163	    from astrid.core.schema_packs.manifest import load_schema_pack_manifest
   164	
   165	    mounts: list[ManifestMount] = []
   166	    for pack_id in _STANDARD_PACK_DIRS:
   167	        manifest = load_schema_pack_manifest(
   168	            _PACKS_ROOT / pack_id / "schema-pack.yaml"
   169	        )
   170	        for family, token in manifest.cli_mounts.items():
   171	            mounts.append(
   172	                ManifestMount(family=str(family), token=str(token), pack_id=pack_id)
   173	            )
   174	    return tuple(mounts)

     3	
     4	Lists every executor, orchestrator, and element with its short_description so
     5	agents can discover what's available without grepping manifests. Idempotent:

     7	
     8	Pass --target to write only the specified file (for testing).
     9	"""

    11	from __future__ import annotations
    12	
    13	import argparse
    14	import sys
    15	from pathlib import Path
    16	
    17	REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    18	if str(REPO_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    19	    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))
    20	
    21	from astrid.core.element.registry import load_default_registry as load_elements  # noqa: E402
    22	from astrid.core.execution.executor.registry import load_default_registry as load_executors  # noqa: E402
    23	from astrid.core.execution.orchestrator.registry import (  # noqa: E402
    24	    load_default_registry as load_orchestrators,
    25	)
    26	from astrid.core.search import short_description_or_truncated  # noqa: E402
    27	from astrid.core.foundation.paths import REPO_ROOT as ASTRID_REPO_ROOT  # noqa: E402
    28	
    29	CORE_SKILL_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "astrid" / "packs" / "_core" / "skill" / "SKILL.md"
    30	
    31	BEGIN_MARKER = "<!-- BEGIN CAPABILITY INDEX (auto-generated by scripts/gen_capability_index.py) -->"
    32	END_MARKER = "<!-- END CAPABILITY INDEX -->"
    33	
    34	
    35	def _row(identifier: str, short: str) -> str:
    36	    cleaned = short.replace("|", "\\|")
    37	    return f"| `{identifier}` | {cleaned} |"
    38	
    39	
    40	def _section(title: str, items: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> list[str]:
    41	    lines = [f"### {title}", "", "| id | short_description |", "| --- | --- |"]
    42	    if not items:
    43	        lines.append("| _(none)_ | |")
    44	    else:
    45	        for identifier, short in sorted(items, key=lambda pair: pair[0]):
    46	            lines.append(_row(identifier, short or "_(no description)_"))
    47	    lines.append("")
    48	    return lines
    49	
    50	
    51	def _executor_rows() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    52	    registry = load_executors()
    53	    return [
    54	        (executor.id, short_description_or_truncated(executor.short_description, executor.description))
    55	        for executor in registry.list()
    56	    ]
    57	
    58	
    59	def _orchestrator_rows() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    60	    registry = load_orchestrators()
    61	    return [
    62	        (orchestrator.id, short_description_or_truncated(orchestrator.short_description, orchestrator.description))
    63	        for orchestrator in registry.list()
    64	    ]
    65	
    66	
    67	def _element_rows() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    68	    registry = load_elements(active_theme=None, project_root=ASTRID_REPO_ROOT)
    69	    return [
    70	        (
    71	            f"{element.kind}/{element.id}",
    72	            short_description_or_truncated(element.short_description, element.description),
    73	        )
    74	        for element in registry.list()
    75	    ]
    76	
    77	
    78	def render_block() -> str:
    79	    lines = [BEGIN_MARKER, ""]
    80	    lines.extend(_section("Executors", _executor_rows()))
    81	    lines.extend(_section("Orchestrators", _orchestrator_rows()))
    82	    lines.extend(_section("Elements", _element_rows()))
    83	    lines.append(END_MARKER)
    84	    return "\n".join(lines)
    85	
    86	
    87	def update_skill(text: str, block: str) -> str:
    88	    if BEGIN_MARKER in text and END_MARKER in text:
    89	        before, _, rest = text.partition(BEGIN_MARKER)
    90	        _, _, after = rest.partition(END_MARKER)
    91	        return f"{before}{block}{after}"
    92	    # Insert before the "## Make something new" heading if present, otherwise
    93	    # append to the end with a leading blank line.
    94	    anchor = "## Make something new"
    95	    if anchor in text:
    96	        before, _, after = text.partition(anchor)
    97	        return f"{before}{block}\n\n{anchor}{after}"
    98	    suffix = "" if text.endswith("\n") else "\n"
    99	    return f"{text}{suffix}\n{block}\n"
   100	
   101	
   102	def main() -> int:
   103	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
   104	    parser.add_argument(
   105	        "--target",
   106	        type=Path,
   107	        default=None,
   108	        help="Write only to the specified file (bypasses deduplication).",
   109	    )
   110	    args = parser.parse_args()
   111	
   112	    block = render_block()
   113	
   114	    targets = [args.target if args.target is not None else CORE_SKILL_PATH]
   115	
   116	    any_updated = False
   117	    for path in targets:
   118	        if not path.exists():
   119	            # Create the file with empty content if it doesn't exist
   120	            current = ""
   121	        else:
   122	            current = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
   123	        updated = update_skill(current, block)
   124	        if updated != current:
   125	            path.write_text(updated, encoding="utf-8")
   126	            print(f"updated {path}")
   127	            any_updated = True
   128	        else:
   129	            print(f"unchanged {path}")
   130	    return 0 if any_updated else 0
   131	
   132	
   133	if __name__ == "__main__":
   134	    raise SystemExit(main())

    61	def _validate_pack_path(path: Path, must_exist: bool = True) -> Path:
    62	    """Resolve and validate a pack root directory path.
    63	
    64	    Args:
    65	        path: The path to resolve.
    66	        must_exist: If True, require the directory to exist.
    67	
    68	    Returns:
    69	        The resolved Path.
    70	
    71	    Raises:
    72	        SystemExit(2) on invalid paths.
    73	    """
    74	    resolved = path.resolve()
    75	    if must_exist and not resolved.is_dir():
    76	        raise AstridError(
    77	            f"packs validate: {path} is not a directory or does not exist",
    78	            recovery_command=f"ls -d {path}  # verify the path exists and is a directory",
    79	        )
    80	    return resolved

   155	    for field, value in _taxonomy_filters(args).items():

   161	def _filtered_packs(
   162	    args: argparse.Namespace, *, include_hidden: bool | None = None
   163	) -> list[PackDefinition]:
   164	    show_hidden = bool(getattr(args, "show_hidden", False))
   165	    roots = [packs_root()]

   167	        *tuple(getattr(args, "pack_roots", None) or ()),
   168	        *(item for item in os.environ.get("ASTRID_PACKS_PATH", "").split(os.pathsep) if item),
   169	    ]
   170	    roots.extend(Path(item).expanduser() for item in raw_roots)
   171	    packs_by_id: dict[str, PackDefinition] = {}
   172	    for root in roots:
   173	        for pack in discover_packs(
   174	            root,
   175	            include_hidden=show_hidden if include_hidden is None else include_hidden,
   176	        ):
   177	            packs_by_id.setdefault(pack.id, pack)
   178	    packs = list(packs_by_id.values())
   179	    category = getattr(args, "category", None)
   180	    status = getattr(args, "status", None)
   181	    visibility = getattr(args, "visibility", None)
   182	    if category:
   183	        packs = [pack for pack in packs if _pack_category(pack) == category]
   184	    packs = [pack for pack in packs if _matches_taxonomy_filters(pack, args)]
   185	    if status:
   186	        packs = [pack for pack in packs if _effective_status(pack) == status]
   187	    if visibility:
   188	        packs = [pack for pack in packs if pack.visibility == visibility]
   189	    return packs

   291	    """Return the validated mount for one registered family.

   323	    """Run one product-family command with the composed *client*.
   324	
   325	    The family's in-tree parser builder is resolved from the static
   326	    :data:`FAMILY_PARSER_MODULES` mapping (never discovered) and receives
   327	    the shared ``AstridClient``; the configured handler then runs with
   328	    zero domain rules in this module. Only the five core families dispatch

   336	            f"exactly {sorted(PRODUCT_FAMILY_SET)}"

   339	    module_name = modules.get(family)

   353	        )

   366	        try:
   367	            selected = selected_project() if callable(selected_project) else None
